# ARTICLE 2 — DEMISE, PREMISES, AND TERM

**Section 2.1 Demise.** Landlord hereby leases the Premises to Tenant, and Tenant hereby leases the Premises from Landlord, for the Term and subject to the covenants, conditions, and provisions of this Lease. The Premises are leased on a triple-net basis, subject only to Landlord's express obligations set forth in this Lease.

**Section 2.2 Premises; Legal Description.** The Premises consist of approximately 3.2 acres (139,392 square feet) of land located at 10-30 Pier Street, Port Calloway, Connecticut 06801, Assessor's Parcel No. 127-003-0045, as more particularly described on **Exhibit A**. The Parties acknowledge that:

> (a) the description set forth on Exhibit A is the metes-and-bounds description derived from the ALTA/NSPS Land Title Survey prepared by Calloway Land Surveyors LLC, Thomas R. Pellegrino, PLS (Connecticut License No. PLS-008741), Survey Job No. CLS-2025-0417, plat dated April 28, 2025 (the **"Survey"**), and certified to Landlord, Tenant, Ridgepoint Title & Escrow Co., and the Leasehold Mortgagee;
>
> (b) the area derived from the Survey's boundary courses (435.22 feet by 320.47 feet) is approximately 139,475 square feet, approximately 83 square feet more than the 139,392 square feet stated above and in the Term Sheet; the Parties agree that the Premises shall be deemed to contain 139,392 square feet for all purposes of this Lease, including the calculation of Base Rent per square foot, and that no adjustment to Base Rent shall be made on account of any discrepancy in area;
>
> (c) the metes-and-bounds description set forth in Exhibit A to Title Commitment No. TC-2025-07821 (effective date June 1, 2025) issued by Ridgepoint Title & Escrow Co. does not conform to the Survey in bearings, distances, or computed area, and Landlord shall cause such description to be conformed to the Survey, and the Issuing Title Company to confirm in writing that its commitment and the Title Policy describe the same parcel, as a condition to the Lease Commencement Date; and
>
> (d) the boundary of the Premises on the south is the northerly line of Assessor's Parcel No. 127-003-0044, as depicted on the Survey. Landlord represents that Assessor's Parcel No. 127-003-0044 is a separate parcel retained by Landlord and is not part of the Premises.

**Section 2.3 Appurtenant Rights.** Together with the Premises, Tenant shall have the right to use, in common with others entitled thereto and subject to the Permitted Exceptions and applicable law: (a) the public rights-of-way abutting the Premises for access and utilities; (b) the public utility easement described in Exhibit C; and (c) such other easements and rights as are appurtenant to the Premises.

**Section 2.4 Term.** The term of this Lease (the **"Term"**) shall commence on October 1, 2025, or such later date as is determined in accordance with Section 2.5 (the **"Lease Commencement Date"**), and shall expire at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on September 30, 2124 (the **"Expiration Date"**), unless sooner terminated as provided in this Lease. The Term is ninety-nine (99) years. Tenant acknowledges that the Term Sheet provided that no renewal or extension options were contemplated and that the ninety-nine (99) year Term constitutes the full duration of this Lease, subject only to Section 20.5.

**Section 2.5 Lease Commencement Date; Conditions Precedent.** The Lease Commencement Date shall be October 1, 2025, or, if later, the first day of the first calendar month following satisfaction or written waiver (by the party entitled to waive) of each of the following conditions precedent:

> (a) execution and delivery of this Lease by both Parties;
>
> (b) delivery by Ridgepoint Title & Escrow Co. (or another nationally recognized title insurance company reasonably acceptable to Tenant) (the **"Issuing Title Company"**) of a commitment, marked to issue, for an ALTA Leasehold Owner's Policy (2006 form, as amended) in the amount of $425,000,000 insuring Tenant's leasehold estate, and an ALTA Leasehold Loan Policy (2006 form, as amended) in the amount of $285,000,000 insuring the Leasehold Mortgagee's first-priority lien, in each case subject only to the Permitted Exceptions and such other exceptions as Tenant has approved in its reasonable discretion, and including the ALTA 13-06 (Leasehold — Owner's) and ALTA 13.1-06 (Leasehold — Loan) endorsements;
>
> (c) delivery of the Survey and the Surveyor's certification, and delivery of an updated survey if and to the extent required by the Leasehold Mortgagee;
>
> (d) delivery by Tenant of the LOC in the amount of $5,700,000 in accordance with Article 10;
>
> (e) execution and delivery by Landlord and the Leasehold Mortgagee of the SNDA;
>
> (f) delivery by Landlord of evidence reasonably satisfactory to Tenant that the mechanics' lien filed by Calloway Marine Demolition Inc. on April 3, 2025 in the amount of $187,500, recorded at Volume 418, Page 302 of the Port Calloway Land Records (the **"Calloway Lien"**), has been discharged of record, bonded over in compliance with Conn. Gen. Stat. § 49-37, or otherwise insured over by the Issuing Title Company without exception (the **"Lien Condition"**);
>
> (g) delivery by Landlord of a certified copy of Resolution No. 2025-047, certified by the Chair and attested by the Executive Director, together with a certificate of the Executive Director that the resolution has not been amended, modified, or rescinded and that the execution and delivery of this Lease have been duly authorized;
>
> (h) delivery by Landlord of an executed Tax Abatement Agreement, duly approved by the City and effective as of the Rent Commencement Date;
>
> (i) delivery by Tenant of (i) a certificate of good standing of Tenant issued by the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware dated not more than thirty (30) days prior to the Lease Commencement Date, (ii) a certificate of authority to transact business issued by the Secretary of the State of Connecticut, and (iii) a certificate of the Managing Member of Tenant certifying the resolutions or written consents of Tenant's members authorizing the execution and delivery of this Lease and the Leasehold Mortgage;
>
> (j) receipt by Tenant of final site plan approval and such zoning approvals, special permits, and variances as are required for the Project as described in Section 4.7; and
>
> (k) delivery by Landlord of the Bulkhead Assessment contemplated by Section 4.11.

If any condition precedent set forth in this Section 2.5 has not been satisfied or waived on or before March 31, 2026 (the **"Conditions Outside Date"**), then either Party may, by written notice to the other delivered before such condition is satisfied, terminate this Lease, whereupon the LOC shall be returned to Tenant within ten (10) Business Days, each Party shall bear its own costs, and neither Party shall have any further obligation to the other except for those obligations that expressly survive termination. The Conditions Outside Date shall be extended day-for-day for Unavoidable Delay affecting satisfaction of such conditions.

**Section 2.6 Delivery of Possession.** Landlord shall deliver exclusive possession of the Premises to Tenant on the Lease Commencement Date, free and clear of all tenancies, occupants, liens (other than Permitted Exceptions), and encumbrances, and in the condition required by Article 3.

**Section 2.7 Memorandum of Lease; Recording.** The Parties shall execute, acknowledge, and record a Memorandum of Lease substantially in the form attached as Exhibit D in the Port Calloway Land Records simultaneously with the execution of this Lease. The Memorandum of Lease shall not disclose the economic terms of this Lease other than the Term, the Base Rent, and the identity of the Parties. Tenant may, at its election, record this Lease in its entirety if and to the extent required by the Leasehold Mortgagee or applicable law. Each Party shall execute such further recordable instruments as are reasonably requested to evidence the existence of this Lease, including any instrument required by the Issuing Title Company.

**Section 2.8 No Merger.** There shall be no merger of the leasehold estate created by this Lease with the fee estate in the Premises by reason of the fact that the same Person may hold or acquire, directly or indirectly, both such estates, unless and until the holder of both estates has executed and recorded a written instrument expressly effecting such merger.

**Section 2.9 Landlord's Reserved Rights.** Landlord reserves the right, without liability to Tenant and without constituting an eviction or disturbance of Tenant's use or possession, to enter upon the Premises at reasonable times and upon not less than ten (10) Business Days' prior written notice (except in the case of an emergency, in which case no notice shall be required) for the purpose of inspecting the Premises, performing any obligation of Landlord that Tenant has failed to perform after notice and the expiration of any applicable cure period, or exercising any right reserved to Landlord under this Lease. Any such entry shall be conducted so as not to unreasonably interfere with Tenant's construction or operations, and Landlord shall repair any damage caused by such entry at its sole cost.

# ARTICLE 3 — TITLE, CONDITION, AND TITLE INSURANCE

**Section 3.1 Condition of Premises.** Except as expressly set forth in this Lease, Tenant accepts the Premises in their "AS IS, WHERE IS" condition as of the Lease Commencement Date. **Notwithstanding the foregoing, the "AS IS" acceptance shall not apply to, and Tenant does not waive, and Landlord expressly warrants, represents, and covenants as to, the following:**

> (a) Landlord's fee simple title to the Premises, free and clear of all liens, encumbrances, and defects other than the Permitted Exceptions;
>
> (b) the absence of any pending or, to Landlord's knowledge, threatened condemnation, rezoning, or governmental taking affecting the Premises;
>
> (c) Landlord's compliance with its obligations under Article 3.6 with respect to the Calloway Lien;
>
> (d) the environmental matters addressed in Section 9.1;
>
> (e) the structural condition of the Bulkhead as addressed in Section 4.11; and
>
> (f) the sufficiency of the Premises, together with the Permitted Exceptions, to support the Project as contemplated by Section 4.7.

**Section 3.2 Landlord's Title Representations and Warranties.** Landlord represents and warrants to Tenant as of the Effective Date and as of the Lease Commencement Date that: (a) Landlord is the sole fee simple owner of the Premises; (b) Landlord has good right and lawful authority to lease the Premises for the Term; (c) the execution and delivery of this Lease have been duly authorized by all necessary action of Landlord, and the persons executing this Lease on behalf of Landlord are duly authorized officers of Landlord; (d) this Lease is a valid, binding, and enforceable obligation of Landlord, subject to applicable bankruptcy and equitable principles; (e) there is no pending or, to Landlord's knowledge, threatened litigation, action, or proceeding affecting the Premises or the validity of this Lease; (f) Landlord has not granted any option, right of first refusal, lease, license, or other right to lease or acquire the Premises or any interest therein, other than the matters described in Exhibit C; (g) Landlord has no knowledge of any undisclosed environmental condition at the Premises other than those disclosed in the Phase I and Phase II Environmental Site Assessments and the ELUR; and (h) Landlord has delivered to Tenant true and complete copies of all documents in Landlord's possession or control relating to title to the Premises, including the 2012 Final Judgment of Condemnation, the recorded easements described in Exhibit C, the ELUR, the recorded Declaration of Right of First Refusal (Volume 405, Page 55), and the recorded Declaration of Restrictive Covenants (Volume 408, Page 230).

**Section 3.3 Permitted Exceptions.** Tenant's leasehold estate is subject to the Permitted Exceptions listed on Exhibit C and to the matters permitted by this Lease. **Landlord covenants to remove or cause to be removed from the title to the Premises (or cause the Issuing Title Company to insure over without exception) each of the following, at Landlord's sole cost and expense, on or before the Lease Commencement Date:**

> (a) the Calloway Lien, in accordance with Section 3.6;
>
> (b) any matter disclosed by the Survey that constitutes an encroachment by adjoining property onto the Premises, or an encroachment by the Bulkhead or other improvements of Landlord onto the Premises;
>
> (c) any judgment, lis pendens, federal or state tax lien, or other lien arising from acts or omissions of Landlord or its predecessors; and
>
> (d) any other matter objected to by Tenant or the Leasehold Mortgagee that is not a Permitted Exception.

**Section 3.4 [Reserved]**

**Section 3.5 Title Policy.** Tenant shall obtain, at its cost, an ALTA Leasehold Owner's Policy and, on behalf of the Leasehold Mortgagee, an ALTA Leasehold Loan Policy from the Issuing Title Company, in the amounts and forms described in Section 2.5(b). **Landlord shall cooperate with Tenant, at no cost to Landlord other than its own attorney's fees, to cause the issuance of the Title Policies with all endorsements reasonably required by Tenant and the Leasehold Mortgagee, and shall execute such affidavits, indemnities, and certificates as the Issuing Title Company may reasonably require.** If the Issuing Title Company requires an affidavit or indemnity from Landlord to eliminate the standard printed exceptions (including the survey exception and the rights of parties in possession exception), Landlord shall deliver the same in a form reasonably acceptable to Landlord.

**Section 3.6 Calloway Lien.** The Parties acknowledge that the Calloway Lien was filed against Landlord's fee interest for bulkhead demolition work performed on the Premises before any interest in the Premises was conveyed or leased to Tenant, and that the Calloway Lien is not the responsibility of Tenant. Landlord shall, at its sole cost and expense, cause the Calloway Lien to be discharged of record, bonded over pursuant to Conn. Gen. Stat. § 49-37 in a penal sum sufficient to cover the lien plus interest and costs, or otherwise insured over without exception, on or before the Lease Commencement Date. Landlord shall indemnify, defend, and hold Tenant and the Leasehold Mortgagee harmless from and against all loss, cost, and expense (including reasonable attorneys' fees) arising from or relating to the Calloway Lien, the underlying work, or any claim by Calloway Marine Demolition Inc. or its successors or assigns. **Landlord's obligations under this Section 3.6 shall survive the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease.**

**Section 3.7 Survey.** Tenant has caused the Survey to be prepared and certified as described in Section 2.2. If the Leasehold Mortgagee, the Issuing Title Company, or applicable law requires an updated or re-certified survey (including an update required to satisfy the ninety (90)-day recency condition customarily imposed by construction lenders), the cost shall be borne by Tenant.

**Section 3.8 Covenant of Quiet Enjoyment and Warranty of Title.** Landlord covenants that so long as no Event of Default by Tenant has occurred and is continuing, Tenant shall peaceably and quietly have, hold, and enjoy the Premises and the Improvements during the Term without hindrance, ejection, or molestation by Landlord or any Person lawfully claiming by, through, or under Landlord, subject to the terms of this Lease. Any Person acquiring the fee interest in the Premises from Landlord, whether by purchase, foreclosure, exercise of a power of sale, deed in lieu of foreclosure, operation of law, or otherwise, shall take the fee interest subject to this Lease and shall recognize Tenant's leasehold estate.

**Section 3.9 Fee Estate Encumbrances.** **Landlord shall not, during the Term, grant or suffer any mortgage, deed of trust, lien, pledge, or other voluntary encumbrance of its fee interest in the Premises, other than a fee mortgage that (a) by its terms is expressly subordinate and junior to this Lease, and (b) is subject to a subordination and non-disturbance agreement, in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to Tenant and each Leasehold Mortgagee, pursuant to which the fee mortgagee recognizes this Lease and agrees that Tenant's leasehold estate and the Leasehold Mortgage shall not be disturbed in the event of foreclosure of the fee mortgage.** Any encumbrance of the fee interest that does not comply with this Section 3.9 shall be void as against Tenant and the Leasehold Mortgagee and shall not affect this Lease. **Section 3.10 Landlord Consent to Collateral Assignments.** Landlord acknowledges that Tenant intends to execute and deliver to the Leasehold Mortgagee a first-priority collateral assignment of all subleases, leases, rents, revenues, and other income arising from the Project, an assignment of construction contracts and plans, and a pledge of Tenant's ownership interests. **Landlord consents to each such assignment and pledge without the need for any further consent, approval, or joinder of Landlord and without the payment of any consent fee, administrative charge, or other compensation, and Landlord agrees that none of the foregoing shall constitute a Transfer requiring Landlord's consent or triggering the Right of First Refusal described in Article 18.**

**Section 4.1 Development Obligation.** Tenant shall develop, construct, and operate the Project on the Premises substantially in accordance with the plans and specifications approved in connection with the site plan approvals referenced in Section 4.7, and in compliance with this Lease, the ELUR, and applicable law. > (a) the eight thousand (8,000) square feet requirement is a minimum net usable area of open space and shall be satisfied notwithstanding the approximate area of the fifteen (15)-foot public pedestrian access easement, which the Parties acknowledge may comprise substantially less than 8,000 square feet given the length of the Premises' eastern boundary; accordingly, the open space may extend inland from the easement area to the extent consistent with the approved site plan;
>
> (b) the design and programming of the open space shall be subject to Landlord's reasonable approval in connection with site plan review, which approval shall be deemed given if Landlord has not objected in writing within fifteen (15) Business Days;
>
> (c) Tenant's obligation to maintain the open space shall be satisfied by maintaining it in a clean, safe, and usable condition consistent with the standards applicable to the adjacent public promenade; and
>
> (d) if the City or Landlord elects to assume maintenance of the open space, Tenant shall remain responsible for structural repairs to the Improvements beneath and adjacent to the open space, and Tenant's maintenance obligation shall terminate as of the date of such assumption.

**Section 4.9 Affordable Housing.** Tenant shall cause not fewer than fifteen percent (15%) of the residential dwelling units in the Project to be designated as affordable housing units available to households earning at or below eighty percent (80%) of area median income as published annually by the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development for the applicable Port Calloway metropolitan statistical area, for the duration of the Affordable Housing Period (as defined in Section 11.5), in accordance with Section 11.5 and Exhibit K.

**Section 4.10 Waterfront Promenade.** Tenant acknowledges the fifteen (15)-foot public pedestrian access easement recorded at Volume 395, Page 112 of the Port Calloway Land Records and shall preserve public pedestrian access within the easement area. Tenant shall not construct permanent structures within the easement area, but may install landscaping, paving, benches, lighting, and similar public amenities consistent with the City's waterfront promenade design standards. Tenant shall comply with the maintenance standards applicable to the promenade.

**Section 4.11 Bulkhead.** The Parties acknowledge that the Bulkhead is a pre-existing waterfront structure that is in fair to poor condition, as described in the Survey and in the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment, and that the cost of rehabilitating or replacing the Bulkhead was expressly excluded from the $2,400,000 environmental remediation cost estimate and is not a part of the Remediation.

> (a) **Bulkhead Assessment.** On or before the Lease Commencement Date, Landlord shall deliver to Tenant an independent structural engineering assessment of the Bulkhead, prepared by a Connecticut-licensed professional engineer reasonably acceptable to Tenant, addressing the condition, remaining useful life, code compliance, and scope and estimated cost of rehabilitation or replacement (the **"Bulkhead Assessment"**).
>
> (b) **Landlord Responsibility for Pre-Existing Condition.** **Landlord shall, at its sole cost and expense (and not as a Remedy of Tenant), be responsible for the rehabilitation or replacement of those portions of the Bulkhead that the Bulkhead Assessment identifies as deficient as a result of conditions existing as of the Lease Commencement Date, including lateral displacement, cracking, deteriorated or missing lagging, corrosion of sheet piling, and erosion of backfill, up to a cost of $4,500,000.** If the Bulkhead Assessment estimates the cost of such rehabilitation or replacement at more than $4,500,000, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith an equitable allocation, and pending resolution Tenant may proceed with the work and receive a rent credit in accordance with Section 4.11(d).
>
> (c) **Tenant Responsibility.** Tenant shall be responsible for the cost of any rehabilitation, replacement, or repair of the Bulkhead required by Tenant's construction means and methods, by changes in applicable law after the Lease Commencement Date, or arising from the condition of the Bulkhead after the Lease Commencement Date (ordinary wear and tear excepted).
>
> (d) **Rent Credit.** If Landlord fails to perform its obligations under Section 4.11(b) and Tenant performs such work, Tenant shall be entitled to a credit against Base Rent, applied in the manner described in Section 9.6, in the amount of the lesser of (i) the actual cost incurred by Tenant and (ii) $4,500,000, together with interest at the rate set forth in Section 6.8 from the date of expenditure.
>
> (e) **Ongoing Obligation.** Following completion of the work described in Sections 4.11(b) and 4.11(c), Tenant shall maintain the Bulkhead in good repair and condition throughout the Term, subject to Casualty and Condemnation.
>
> (f) **No Conflict with ELUR.** All Bulkhead work shall be performed in compliance with the ELUR and any required DEEP approvals.

**Section 4.12 Below-Grade Work and Dewatering.** The Parties acknowledge that the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment's remediation cost estimates assume that groundwater dewatering and treatment will not be required during excavation. Tenant may, but shall not be obligated to, construct below-grade parking. Tenant shall obtain all required DEEP and municipal approvals for dewatering and discharge.

# ARTICLE 5 — MILESTONE DEFAULT, REVERTER RIGHT, AND COMPENSATION FOR IMPROVEMENTS

**Section 5.1 The Reverter Right.** If Tenant fails to achieve Milestone 1 or Milestone 3 (in each case as extended pursuant to Sections 4.3 and 4.4), Landlord may, subject to and only in strict compliance with this Article 5, elect to terminate this Lease and cause the Premises and the Improvements to revert to Landlord (the **"Reverter Right"**). The Reverter Right is subject to each of the following conditions precedent, each of which is a **condition precedent to the effectiveness of any termination under this Article 5** and each of which must be satisfied in full:

> (a) **Milestone Failure.** Tenant has failed to achieve Milestone 1 or Milestone 3, as extended;
>
> (b) **Milestone Default Notice.** Landlord has delivered to Tenant and, simultaneously, to each Leasehold Mortgagee a written notice (a **"Milestone Default Notice"**) specifying in reasonable detail the Milestone alleged not to have been achieved and the factual basis for that assertion;
>
> (c) **Tenant Cure Period Expired.** The Milestone Cure Period has expired without Tenant having achieved the applicable Milestone;
>
> (d) **Leasehold Mortgagee Notice and Cure Period Expired.** Each Leasehold Mortgagee has received the Milestone Default Notice simultaneously with Tenant, and the Mortgagee Cure Period applicable to such Leasehold Mortgagee has expired without cure in accordance with Section 5.4;
>
> (e) **Improvement Compensation Determined and Paid.** The Improvement Compensation has been determined in accordance with Section 5.6 and paid in full to Tenant and, to the extent of the Indebtedness, to the Leasehold Mortgagee in accordance with Section 5.5; and
>
> (f) **Mediation.** The mediation requirement of Section 5.9 has been satisfied.

**Section 5.2 Milestone Default Notice; Tenant Cure Period.** Upon delivery of a Milestone Default Notice, Tenant shall have one hundred eighty (180) days (the **"Milestone Cure Period"**) to achieve the applicable Milestone or otherwise cure the alleged failure. **The Milestone Cure Period is in addition to, and shall not run concurrently with, the extensions available under Sections 4.3 and 4.4.**

**Section 5.3 [Reserved]**

**Section 5.4 Leasehold Mortgagee Notice and Cure.** **Landlord shall not deliver a notice of termination, shall not declare this Lease terminated, and shall not exercise the Reverter Right, unless and until each Leasehold Mortgagee has received the Milestone Default Notice simultaneously with Tenant and has been afforded, and has failed to exercise, the following rights:**

> (a) **Notice.** Simultaneous delivery of the Milestone Default Notice, and of every other notice of default, notice of termination, and material notice delivered to Tenant under this Lease, to each Leasehold Mortgagee at the address designated by such Leasehold Mortgagee in accordance with Section 17.3.

> (b) **Mortgagee Cure Period.** A period of one hundred eighty (180) days following the Leasehold Mortgagee's receipt of the Milestone Default Notice (the **"Mortgagee Cure Period"**) within which the Leasehold Mortgagee may cure the Milestone default. **The Mortgagee Cure Period shall run in addition to, and not concurrently with, the Milestone Cure Period available to Tenant and any extension available under Section 4.3 or 4.4.**

> (c) **Manner of Cure.** The Leasehold Mortgagee may cure a Milestone default by any of the following means, in its sole discretion: (i) performing or causing the performance of all work necessary to achieve the applicable Milestone; (ii) paying all sums necessary to achieve the applicable Milestone; (iii) installing a replacement developer, general contractor, or property manager reasonably acceptable to Landlord (which acceptance shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, and which shall be deemed given if Landlord has not objected in writing within ten (10) Business Days after receiving notice of the proposed replacement); or (iv) exercising its rights under Section 17.5.

> (d) **Landlord Cooperation.** Landlord shall accept performance by a Leasehold Mortgagee as if performed by Tenant and shall execute all documents reasonably necessary to permit such cure, including any assignment or assumption of development rights, permits, and contracts.

> (e) **No Termination Without Exhaustion.** The expiration of the Mortgagee Cure Period without cure is a **hard prerequisite** to any termination of this Lease or exercise of the Reverter Right, and any purported termination effected before such expiration shall be void and of no force or effect.

> (f) **Consent.** If the Leasehold Mortgagee has delivered written notice to Landlord that it intends to exercise its rights under this Section 5.4, Landlord shall not exercise the Reverter Right without the prior written consent of such Leasehold Mortgagee.

**Section 5.5 Compensation for Improvements.** **Upon any termination of this Lease pursuant to this Article 5 (a "Reverter Termination"), Tenant shall be entitled to receive, and Landlord shall pay, compensation for the Improvements (the "Improvement Compensation") determined as follows:**

> (a) **Tenant's Election.** Tenant may elect, by written notice delivered to Landlord within thirty (30) days after the determination of the Appraised Value, to receive either:
>
> > (i) the **Appraised Value** of the Improvements as of the effective date of the Reverter Termination, determined in accordance with Section 5.6; or
> >
> > (ii) an amount equal to Tenant's **actual, unreimbursed Hard Costs and Soft Costs** of the Improvements incurred as of the effective date of the Reverter Termination, net of (A) any insurance proceeds received by Tenant on account of the Improvements and not applied to restoration, and (B) the amount of Landlord's actual, documented damages (excluding consequential, indirect, punitive, and speculative damages, and excluding the value of the reversion or of any lost rent or lost land value) resulting from Tenant's failure to achieve the applicable Milestone.
>
> (b) **Floor.** In no event shall the Improvement Compensation be less than the outstanding principal balance of, and accrued interest and other amounts owing under, the Indebtedness secured by the Leasehold Mortgage as of the effective date of the Reverter Termination, up to the Appraised Value of the Improvements.
>
> (c) **Payee.** Landlord shall pay the Improvement Compensation to Tenant and, at the election of the Leasehold Mortgagee (or as required under the SNDA), shall pay all or any portion thereof directly to the Leasehold Mortgagee in satisfaction of the Indebtedness. Payment to the Leasehold Mortgagee shall discharge Landlord's obligation to Tenant to the extent of such payment.

**Section 5.6 Determination of Appraised Value.** The Appraised Value of the Improvements shall be determined as follows:

> (a) Within thirty (30) days after the delivery of a Milestone Default Notice, Landlord and Tenant shall jointly select an independent MAI-designated appraiser licensed in Connecticut and having not less than ten (10) years' experience appraising mixed-use waterfront properties in the Northeast (the **"Appraiser"**), who shall determine the fair market value of the Improvements as of the effective date of the proposed Reverter Termination, determined as the value attributable to the Improvements alone, excluding the value of the land and excluding any value attributable to the fact that the land is owned by Landlord, and assuming a willing buyer and a willing seller and a reasonable marketing period.
>
> (b) The Appraiser's determination shall be delivered to both Parties within forty-five (45) days after engagement, shall be in writing and supported by an explanation of methodology, and shall be final and binding on the Parties absent manifest error or fraud.
>
> (c) If the Parties cannot agree on the Appraiser within such thirty (30) day period, each Party shall select an appraiser meeting the foregoing qualifications, each such appraiser shall determine the Appraised Value within forty-five (45) days, and if the two determinations differ by more than ten percent (10%) of the higher determination, the two appraisers shall jointly select a third appraiser meeting the same qualifications whose determination within thirty (30) days shall be final and binding and whose determination shall be the Appraised Value. If the two determinations differ by ten percent (10%) or less, the Appraised Value shall be the average of the two.
>
> (d) The fees and expenses of the Appraiser shall be borne by Landlord if Tenant elects the option in Section 5.5(a)(i), and shall be shared equally if Tenant elects the option in Section 5.5(a)(ii).

**Section 5.7 Effect of Non-Payment; No Forfeiture.** **No Reverter Termination shall be effective, and this Lease shall not terminate, unless and until Landlord has paid the Improvement Compensation in full in immediately available funds in accordance with Section 5.5.** If Landlord fails to pay the Improvement Compensation within sixty (60) days after its determination (or if the amount is not disputed in good faith, within sixty (60) days after the delivery of Tenant's election), then:

> (a) the Milestone Default giving rise to the Milestone Default Notice shall be deemed conclusively waived and of no further effect;
>
> (b) this Lease shall continue in full force and effect as if no Milestone Default Notice had been delivered;
>
> (c) Landlord shall have no further right to deliver a Milestone Default Notice with respect to the same Milestone failure; and
>
> (d) Tenant shall have no obligation to vacate or surrender the Premises.

**Section 5.8 Improvements Not Forfeited; Security Deposit.** **Tenant shall not forfeit the Improvements or any interest therein upon any termination of this Lease, whether under this Article 5 or otherwise, except upon the expiration of the Term in accordance with Article 20.** Upon a Reverter Termination, Landlord may draw upon the Security Deposit only to the extent of Landlord's actual, documented damages (if any) and shall return the balance to Tenant within thirty (30) days after the draw. **In no event shall Landlord recover, in respect of a single Milestone failure, both (i) the full amount of the Security Deposit and (ii) the Improvements without payment of the Improvement Compensation, and in no event shall Landlord's aggregate recovery in respect of a Milestone failure exceed its actual, documented damages plus the value of the reversion of the land.**

**Section 5.9 Mediation.** Before exercising the Reverter Right, Landlord shall submit the dispute to non-binding mediation in accordance with Section 23.2. The mediation shall be commenced within thirty (30) days after the expiration of the Mortgagee Cure Period and shall be concluded within sixty (60) days after commencement. **The Reverter Right may not be exercised while mediation is pending, and Tenant's obligations under this Lease (including its obligation to continue developing the Project) shall continue during the mediation.**

**Section 5.10 Exclusive Remedies for Milestone Failure.** Landlord's remedies for a failure to achieve Milestone 1 or Milestone 3 are limited to (a) the Reverter Right, exercised in strict compliance with this Article 5, and (b) an action for specific performance of Tenant's development obligations. **Landlord shall have no right to (i) terminate this Lease except pursuant to Article 5, (ii) take title to the Improvements without payment of the Improvement Compensation, (iii) accelerate any Rent, (iv) recover liquidated or punitive damages, or (v) recover consequential or indirect damages in respect of a Milestone failure.**

**Section 5.11 Nature of the Improvement Compensation; No Penalty.** The Parties acknowledge and agree that: (a) the Improvements will represent an investment by Tenant of several hundred million dollars; (b) the Improvement Compensation is intended to compensate Tenant for the value of Improvements that will become Landlord's property, and is not a liquidated damages provision, a penalty, or a forfeiture; (c) the amount payable under Section 5.5 is intended to approximate the value of what Tenant loses and what Landlord receives, and is not grossly disproportionate to the harm, if any, suffered by Landlord; and (d) if any provision of this Article 5 is determined to be unenforceable as a penalty or forfeiture, the remaining provisions shall be enforced to the maximum extent permitted by law, and Landlord shall in any event pay Tenant the fair value of the Improvements as a condition to receiving title to them.

**Section 5.12 No Waiver by Negotiation.** Neither Party's participation in mediation, nor any delay by Landlord in delivering a Milestone Default Notice, nor Landlord's acceptance of Rent after a Milestone failure, shall constitute a waiver of the Reverter Right, provided that no Reverter Termination shall be effective except in compliance with this Article 5.

# ARTICLE 6 — BASE RENT

**Section 6.1 Covenant to Pay Base Rent.** Commencing on the Rent Commencement Date, Tenant shall pay to Landlord annual base rent (the **"Base Rent"**) in accordance with this Article 6, in equal monthly installments, in advance, on the first day of each calendar month, without demand, and without setoff, counterclaim, abatement, suspension, deduction, or defense except as expressly provided in this Lease.

**Section 6.2 Initial Base Rent.** The initial annual Base Rent shall be **Two Million Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars ($2,850,000)**, payable in equal monthly installments of **Two Hundred Thirty-Seven Thousand Five Hundred Dollars ($237,500)**. The Parties acknowledge that the initial annual Base Rent equates to approximately $20.45 per square foot of Premises area (based on 139,392 square feet).

**Section 6.3 Rent Commencement Date.** The **"Rent Commencement Date"** means the earlier of:

> (a) October 1, 2028 (being the date thirty-six (36) months after the anticipated Lease Commencement Date of October 1, 2025, and in any event thirty-six (36) months after the actual Lease Commencement Date); or
>
> (b) the date on which a temporary or permanent certificate of occupancy is first issued for at least one hundred (100) residential dwelling units within the Residential Tower.

**Percentage Rent shall not be payable for any period before the Rent Commencement Date.** From the Lease Commencement Date until the Rent Commencement Date, Tenant shall have no obligation to pay Base Rent or Percentage Rent, but shall be responsible for Taxes, insurance premiums, utilities, and other carrying costs of the Premises as provided in this Lease (subject to Article 8.7).

**Section 6.4 Fixed Escalations.** Base Rent for the following Rent Years shall be as set forth below:

| Rent Years | Annual Base Rent | Monthly Installment |
|---|---|---|
| 1 – 5 | $2,850,000 | $237,500 |
| 6 – 10 | $3,224,500 | $268,708.33 |
| 11 – 15 | $3,648,225 | $304,018.75 |

**Section 6.5 CPI Resets.** Effective on each Reset Date, Base Rent shall be reset to the greater of:

> (a) the annual Base Rent in effect immediately prior to such Reset Date, multiplied by 1.025 raised to the tenth power (that is, the annual compounding of two and one-half percent (2.5%) over the ten (10) Rent Years immediately preceding such Reset Date); or
>
> (b) the annual Base Rent in effect immediately prior to such Reset Date, multiplied by a fraction, the numerator of which is the CPI for the calendar month that is three (3) months prior to such Reset Date and the denominator of which is the CPI for the calendar month that is three (3) months prior to the immediately preceding Reset Date (or, for the first Reset Date, the CPI for the calendar month that is three (3) months prior to the Rent Commencement Date); **provided, however, that the increase determined under this clause (b) shall not exceed four percent (4.0%) per annum, compounded over the applicable ten (10) Rent Year period.**

Base Rent shall not be reduced below the amount in effect immediately prior to any Reset Date, and shall not be reduced below the initial annual Base Rent of $2,850,000.

**Section 6.6 CPI Mechanics.**

> (a) The CPI for the calendar month that is three (3) months prior to the Rent Commencement Date (the **"Base CPI"**) shall be stated in a schedule delivered by Tenant to Landlord within thirty (30) days after the Rent Commencement Date and countersigned by Landlord (whose countersignature shall not be unreasonably withheld).
>
> (b) All CPI-based calculations shall be rounded to the nearest cent and shall be based on the CPI as published and not seasonally adjusted.
>
> (c) If the CPI is rebased (that is, the index is re-referenced to a new base year), the Parties shall apply the conversion factor published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics so that the comparison reflects equivalent index levels.
>
> (d) If the CPI ceases to be published and no successor index is published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the Parties shall select a comparable index of consumer prices for the Northeast Region published by a recognized governmental or financial authority; if the Parties cannot agree within thirty (30) days, the selection shall be made by the Appraiser appointed pursuant to Section 5.6(a), whose determination shall be final and binding.

**Section 6.7 Net Lease; Limited Offsets.** This Lease is a net lease, except as expressly provided in this Lease. Notwithstanding Section 6.1, Tenant shall be entitled to offset against Base Rent, and to deduct from any installment of Base Rent, each of the following amounts (each an **"Express Offset"**):

> (a) the Remediation Credit, as provided in Section 9.6;
>
> (b) any credit due under Section 4.11(d) (Bulkhead);
>
> (c) any amount due from Landlord to Tenant under Section 8.8 (Tax Abatement failure), Section 19.5 (Landlord default), or Section 15.2 (Casualty abatement);
>
> (d) any overpayment of Percentage Rent determined under Section 7.8;
>
> (e) any amount expended by Tenant to cure a Landlord default pursuant to Section 19.5, together with interest at the rate set forth in Section 6.8; and
>
> (f) any amount payable by Landlord to Tenant under any indemnity in this Lease.

Tenant shall give Landlord not less than ten (10) Business Days' prior written notice of any Express Offset (except in the case of an emergency), stating the amount and the basis, and Landlord may dispute the offset in accordance with Article 23. Exercise of an Express Offset shall not constitute an Event of Default.

**Section 6.8 Late Payment.** Any installment of Base Rent or other amount payable by Tenant that is not paid within five (5) Business Days after its due date shall bear interest from the due date until paid at the lesser of (a) the rate of eight percent (8%) per annum and (b) the maximum rate permitted by applicable law. No late charge, penalty, or default interest in excess of such rate shall be payable by Tenant. **Any amount payable by Landlord to Tenant under this Lease that is not paid when due shall bear interest at the same rate.**

**Section 6.9 Application of Payments.** Landlord shall apply each payment of Base Rent to the Base Rent then most recently due. Tenant may designate the manner in which any payment is applied where more than one amount is outstanding.

**Section 6.10 Records.** Tenant shall deliver to Landlord, within thirty (30) days after the Rent Commencement Date and within thirty (30) days after each Reset Date, a written statement setting forth the Base Rent then in effect and the calculation thereof. Any computational error in a statement shall be corrected upon written notice, and any overpayment shall be refunded or credited to Tenant within thirty (30) days.
XEOF

> (b) The Appraiser's determination shall be delivered to both Parties within forty-five (45) days after engagement, shall be in writing and supported by an explanation of methodology, and shall be final and binding on the Parties absent manifest error or fraud.
>
> (c) If the Parties cannot agree on the Appraiser within such thirty (30) day period, each Party shall select an appraiser meeting the foregoing qualifications, each such appraiser shall determine the Appraised Value within forty-five (45) days, and if the two determinations differ by more than ten percent (10%) of the higher determination, the two appraisers shall jointly select a third appraiser meeting the same qualifications whose determination within thirty (30) days shall be final and binding and whose determination shall be the Appraised Value. If the two determinations differ by ten percent (10%) or less, the Appraised Value shall be the average of the two.
>
> (d) The fees and expenses of the Appraiser shall be borne by Landlord if Tenant elects the option in Section 5.5(a)(i), and shall be shared equally if Tenant elects the option in Section 5.5(a)(ii).

**Section 5.7 Effect of Non-Payment; No Forfeiture.** **No Reverter Termination shall be effective, and this Lease shall not terminate, unless and until Landlord has paid the Improvement Compensation in full in immediately available funds in accordance with Section 5.5.** If Landlord fails to pay the Improvement Compensation within sixty (60) days after its determination (or if the amount is not disputed in good faith, within sixty (60) days after the delivery of Tenant's election), then:

> (a) the Milestone Default giving rise to the Milestone Default Notice shall be deemed conclusively waived and of no further effect;
>
> (b) this Lease shall continue in full force and effect as if no Milestone Default Notice had been delivered;
>
> (c) Landlord shall have no further right to deliver a Milestone Default Notice with respect to the same Milestone failure; and
>
> (d) Tenant shall have no obligation to vacate or surrender the Premises.

**Section 5.8 Improvements Not Forfeited; Security Deposit.** **Tenant shall not forfeit the Improvements or any interest therein upon any termination of this Lease, whether under this Article 5 or otherwise, except upon the expiration of the Term in accordance with Article 20.** Upon a Reverter Termination, Landlord may draw upon the Security Deposit only to the extent of Landlord's actual, documented damages (if any) and shall return the balance to Tenant within thirty (30) days after the draw. **In no event shall Landlord recover, in respect of a single Milestone failure, both (i) the full amount of the Security Deposit and (ii) the Improvements without payment of the Improvement Compensation, and in no event shall Landlord's aggregate recovery in respect of a Milestone failure exceed its actual, documented damages plus the value of the reversion of the land.**

**Section 5.9 Mediation.** Before exercising the Reverter Right, Landlord shall submit the dispute to non-binding mediation in accordance with Section 23.2. The mediation shall be commenced within thirty (30) days after the expiration of the Mortgagee Cure Period and shall be concluded within sixty (60) days after commencement. **The Reverter Right may not be exercised while mediation is pending, and Tenant's obligations under this Lease (including its obligation to continue developing the Project) shall continue during the mediation.**

**Section 5.10 Exclusive Remedies for Milestone Failure.** Landlord's remedies for a failure to achieve Milestone 1 or Milestone 3 are limited to (a) the Reverter Right, exercised in strict compliance with this Article 5, and (b) an action for specific performance of Tenant's development obligations. **Landlord shall have no right to (i) terminate this Lease except pursuant to Article 5, (ii) take title to the Improvements without payment of the Improvement Compensation, (iii) accelerate any Rent, (iv) recover liquidated or punitive damages, or (v) recover consequential or indirect damages in respect of a Milestone failure.**

**Section 5.11 Nature of the Improvement Compensation; No Penalty.** The Parties acknowledge and agree that: (a) the Improvements will represent an investment by Tenant of several hundred million dollars; (b) the Improvement Compensation is intended to compensate Tenant for the value of Improvements that will become Landlord's property, and is not a liquidated damages provision, a penalty, or a forfeiture; (c) the amount payable under Section 5.5 is intended to approximate the value of what Tenant loses and what Landlord receives, and is not grossly disproportionate to the harm, if any, suffered by Landlord; and (d) if any provision of this Article 5 is determined to be unenforceable as a penalty or forfeiture, the remaining provisions shall be enforced to the maximum extent permitted by law, and Landlord shall in any event pay Tenant the fair value of the Improvements as a condition to receiving title to them.

**Section 5.12 No Waiver by Negotiation.** Neither Party's participation in mediation, nor any delay by Landlord in delivering a Milestone Default Notice, nor Landlord's acceptance of Rent after a Milestone failure, shall constitute a waiver of the Reverter Right, provided that no Reverter Termination shall be effective except in compliance with this Article 5.

# ARTICLE 6 — BASE RENT

**Section 6.1 Covenant to Pay Base Rent.** Commencing on the Rent Commencement Date, Tenant shall pay to Landlord annual base rent (the **"Base Rent"**) in accordance with this Article 6, in equal monthly installments, in advance, on the first day of each calendar month, without demand, and without setoff, counterclaim, abatement, suspension, deduction, or defense except as expressly provided in this Lease.

**Section 6.2 Initial Base Rent.** The initial annual Base Rent shall be **Two Million Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars ($2,850,000)**, payable in equal monthly installments of **Two Hundred Thirty-Seven Thousand Five Hundred Dollars ($237,500)**. The Parties acknowledge that the initial annual Base Rent equates to approximately $20.45 per square foot of Premises area (based on 139,392 square feet).

**Section 6.3 Rent Commencement Date.** The **"Rent Commencement Date"** means the earlier of:

> (a) October 1, 2028 (being the date thirty-six (36) months after the anticipated Lease Commencement Date of October 1, 2025, and in any event thirty-six (36) months after the actual Lease Commencement Date); or
>
> (b) the date on which a temporary or permanent certificate of occupancy is first issued for at least one hundred (100) residential dwelling units within the Residential Tower.

**Percentage Rent shall not be payable for any period before the Rent Commencement Date.** From the Lease Commencement Date until the Rent Commencement Date, Tenant shall have no obligation to pay Base Rent or Percentage Rent, but shall be responsible for Taxes, insurance premiums, utilities, and other carrying costs of the Premises as provided in this Lease (subject to Article 8.7).

**Section 6.4 Fixed Escalations.** Base Rent for the following Rent Years shall be as set forth below:

| Rent Years | Annual Base Rent | Monthly Installment |
|---|---|---|
| 1 – 5 | $2,850,000 | $237,500 |
| 6 – 10 | $3,224,500 | $268,708.33 |
| 11 – 15 | $3,648,225 | $304,018.75 |

**Section 6.5 CPI Resets.** Effective on each Reset Date, Base Rent shall be reset to the greater of:

> (a) the annual Base Rent in effect immediately prior to such Reset Date, multiplied by 1.025 raised to the tenth power (that is, the annual compounding of two and one-half percent (2.5%) over the ten (10) Rent Years immediately preceding such Reset Date); or
>
> (b) the annual Base Rent in effect immediately prior to such Reset Date, multiplied by a fraction, the numerator of which is the CPI for the calendar month that is three (3) months prior to such Reset Date and the denominator of which is the CPI for the calendar month that is three (3) months prior to the immediately preceding Reset Date (or, for the first Reset Date, the CPI for the calendar month that is three (3) months prior to the Rent Commencement Date); **provided, however, that the increase determined under this clause (b) shall not exceed four percent (4.0%) per annum, compounded over the applicable ten (10) Rent Year period.**

Base Rent shall not be reduced below the amount in effect immediately prior to any Reset Date, and shall not be reduced below the initial annual Base Rent of $2,850,000.

**Section 6.6 CPI Mechanics.**

> (a) The CPI for the calendar month that is three (3) months prior to the Rent Commencement Date (the **"Base CPI"**) shall be stated in a schedule delivered by Tenant to Landlord within thirty (30) days after the Rent Commencement Date and countersigned by Landlord (whose countersignature shall not be unreasonably withheld).
>
> (b) All CPI-based calculations shall be rounded to the nearest cent and shall be based on the CPI as published and not seasonally adjusted.
>
> (c) If the CPI is rebased (that is, the index is re-referenced to a new base year), the Parties shall apply the conversion factor published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics so that the comparison reflects equivalent index levels.
>
> (d) If the CPI ceases to be published and no successor index is published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the Parties shall select a comparable index of consumer prices for the Northeast Region published by a recognized governmental or financial authority; if the Parties cannot agree within thirty (30) days, the selection shall be made by the Appraiser appointed pursuant to Section 5.6(a), whose determination shall be final and binding.

**Section 6.7 Net Lease; Limited Offsets.** This Lease is a net lease, except as expressly provided in this Lease. Notwithstanding Section 6.1, Tenant shall be entitled to offset against Base Rent, and to deduct from any installment of Base Rent, each of the following amounts (each an **"Express Offset"**):

> (a) the Remediation Credit, as provided in Section 9.6;
>
> (b) any credit due under Section 4.11(d) (Bulkhead);
>
> (c) any amount due from Landlord to Tenant under Section 8.8 (Tax Abatement failure), Section 19.5 (Landlord default), or Section 15.2 (Casualty abatement);
>
> (d) any overpayment of Percentage Rent determined under Section 7.8;
>
> (e) any amount expended by Tenant to cure a Landlord default pursuant to Section 19.5, together with interest at the rate set forth in Section 6.8; and
>
> (f) any amount payable by Landlord to Tenant under any indemnity in this Lease.

Tenant shall give Landlord not less than ten (10) Business Days' prior written notice of any Express Offset (except in the case of an emergency), stating the amount and the basis, and Landlord may dispute the offset in accordance with Article 23. Exercise of an Express Offset shall not constitute an Event of Default.

**Section 6.8 Late Payment.** Any installment of Base Rent or other amount payable by Tenant that is not paid within five (5) Business Days after its due date shall bear interest from the due date until paid at the lesser of (a) the rate of eight percent (8%) per annum and (b) the maximum rate permitted by applicable law. No late charge, penalty, or default interest in excess of such rate shall be payable by Tenant. **Any amount payable by Landlord to Tenant under this Lease that is not paid when due shall bear interest at the same rate.**

**Section 6.9 Application of Payments.** Landlord shall apply each payment of Base Rent to the Base Rent then most recently due. Tenant may designate the manner in which any payment is applied where more than one amount is outstanding.

**Section 6.10 Records.** Tenant shall deliver to Landlord, within thirty (30) days after the Rent Commencement Date and within thirty (30) days after each Reset Date, a written statement setting forth the Base Rent then in effect and the calculation thereof. Any computational error in a statement shall be corrected upon written notice, and any overpayment shall be refunded or credited to Tenant within thirty (30) days.

# ARTICLE 7 — PERCENTAGE RENT

**Section 7.1 Obligation to Pay Percentage Rent.** Beginning with Rent Year 6 and continuing for the remainder of the Term, Tenant shall pay to Landlord additional rent (**"Percentage Rent"**) equal to two percent (2.0%) of the amount by which the Gross Revenues of the Project for such Rent Year exceed the Breakpoint for such Rent Year. Percentage Rent shall be paid in accordance with Section 7.7.

**Section 7.2 Definition of Gross Revenues.** **"Gross Revenues"** means the total gross revenues actually received by Tenant and its Affiliates from the operation of the Project during the applicable Rent Year, determined on a cash basis, including:

> (a) residential rental income, including base rent, amenity fees, pet fees, parking income attributable to residents, and other residential charges;
>
> (b) office rental income, including base rent and additional rent;
>
> (c) retail rental income, including base rent, additional rent, and percentage rent received from retail subtenants;
>
> (d) parking revenues from the parking facilities within the Project;
>
> (e) income from antenna, rooftop, signage, telecommunications, and similar licenses; and
>
> (f) income from vending, laundry, package lockers, co-working, short-term rental, event, and other ancillary operations conducted at the Premises.

**Section 7.3 Exclusions from Gross Revenues.** Gross Revenues shall **exclude**, and Tenant shall have no obligation to pay Percentage Rent with respect to, each of the following:

> (a) security deposits, except to the extent applied to rent and actually received as revenue;
>
> (b) utility reimbursements and pass-throughs, including recoveries of electricity, gas, water, sewer, trash, and telecommunications charges;
>
> (c) common area maintenance, real estate tax, insurance, and operating expense pass-throughs and recoveries from subtenants, including any administrative or management fee imposed on such pass-throughs;
>
> (d) proceeds of insurance, including business interruption proceeds and proceeds received on account of a Casualty;
>
> (e) condemnation awards;
>
> (f) capital contributions, equity contributions, loans, and other financing proceeds;
>
> (g) proceeds of the sale or other disposition of the Project or any portion thereof or interest therein, and proceeds of any sale of Tenant's leasehold estate;
>
> (h) interest income and investment earnings on reserves and deposits;
>
> (i) lease termination payments, buy-out payments, and settlement proceeds received from subtenants;
>
> (j) amounts received from any warranty, guaranty, indemnity, or claim;
>
> (k) sales, use, occupancy, hotel, and amusement taxes, and any other taxes or governmental charges collected from subtenants and remitted to a taxing authority;
>
> (l) bad debt recoveries to the extent previously written off and excluded from Gross Revenues;
>
> (m) refunds, rebates, and credits (other than refunds of amounts previously included in Gross Revenues);
>
> (n) employee, guest, and resident concession and discount amounts to the extent not collected;
>
> (o) amounts received from the sale of affordable housing tax credits, low-income housing tax credits, or any similar tax incentive;
>
> (p) grants, subsidies, and incentive payments received from any Governmental Authority; and
>
> (q) any amounts that are not true revenue to Tenant, including amounts collected on behalf of third parties.

**In addition, Gross Revenues shall be determined without including any revenue from a business or activity that is not conducted at the Premises.** Tenant may satisfy its obligations under this Article 7 by delivering a statement of Gross Revenues prepared on the same basis as the Project's audited or reviewed annual financial statements, consistently applied.

**Section 7.4 Deductions from Gross Revenues.** In calculating Gross Revenues, Tenant may deduct (a) amounts actually written off as uncollectible during the Rent Year in accordance with Tenant's customary accounting practices, and (b) the amount of any rent concession, free rent, or abatement actually granted to a subtenant.

**Section 7.5 Indexation of the Breakpoint.** **The Breakpoint shall be adjusted on each Reset Date** by multiplying the Breakpoint in effect immediately prior to such Reset Date by the same fraction used to calculate the CPI-based adjustment to Base Rent under Section 6.5(b) for such Reset Date. **In no event shall the Breakpoint be reduced below $28,500,000.** The Breakpoint as so adjusted shall apply to the Rent Year beginning on the applicable Reset Date and to each Rent Year thereafter until the next Reset Date. Tenant shall deliver to Landlord, together with the statement required by Section 6.10, a statement setting forth the Breakpoint as adjusted.

**The Parties acknowledge that the purpose of this Section 7.5 is to preserve over the full ninety-nine (99) year Term the economic relationship between the Breakpoint and project revenues that the Parties negotiated in 2025, so that Percentage Rent operates as a participation in the Project's real growth rather than as a levy on inflationary revenue increases.**

**Section 7.6 Cumulative Adjustment for Non-Reset Periods [Reserved].**

**Section 7.7 Calculation, Statement, and Payment.** Percentage Rent for each Rent Year shall be calculated annually and shall be due and payable within ninety (90) days after the end of such Rent Year. Each payment shall be accompanied by a certified statement of Gross Revenues for the applicable Rent Year, prepared in accordance with Section 7.2 on a basis consistent with the Project's annual financial statements, and signed by an authorized officer of Tenant. **If Tenant fails to deliver the statement and pay any Percentage Rent when due and such failure continues for thirty (30) days after written notice from Landlord, the unpaid amount shall bear interest in accordance with Section 6.8, but such failure shall not of itself constitute an Event of Default until such thirty (30) day period has expired.**

**Section 7.8 Audit.** Landlord shall have the right, exercisable not more than once in any Rent Year and not more than once with respect to any Rent Year, to audit Tenant's books and records relating to Gross Revenues for the two (2) Rent Years most recently ended, upon not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice. Any such audit shall be conducted by an independent certified public accountant reasonably acceptable to Tenant, during normal business hours, at Tenant's principal place of business or remotely, and in a manner that does not unreasonably interfere with the operation of the Project. **The following shall apply to any audit:**

> (a) **Cost.** If the audit discloses an underpayment of Percentage Rent of five percent (5%) or more for the audited Rent Year, Tenant shall reimburse Landlord for the reasonable out-of-pocket cost of the audit. If the audit discloses an underpayment of less than five percent (5%), or discloses an overpayment, Landlord shall bear the full cost of the audit.
>
> (b) **Payment or Credit.** Any underpayment disclosed by an audit shall be paid by Tenant within thirty (30) days after delivery of the auditor's report, together with interest at the rate set forth in Section 6.8 from the original due date. Any overpayment shall be credited against the next installment of Base Rent or, if no further Rent is payable, refunded within thirty (30) days.
>
> (c) **Records.** Tenant shall maintain complete and accurate books and records relating to Gross Revenues for not less than three (3) years following the end of each Rent Year, and Landlord's audit right with respect to any Rent Year shall expire twenty-four (24) months after the delivery of the statement for such Rent Year.
>
> (d) **Confidentiality.** Landlord shall, and shall cause its auditor to, keep all information obtained in any audit confidential and shall not disclose it except to its Board, its attorneys, its auditors, or as required by the Connecticut Freedom of Information Act or other applicable law. Landlord shall assert all available exemptions, including Conn. Gen. Stat. § 1-210(b)(5) (trade secrets and commercial or financial information), before disclosing any such information.
>
> (e) **No Landlord Audit of Subtenant Records.** Landlord's audit right extends only to Tenant's records, and Landlord shall have no right to audit Tenant's subtenants directly.

**Section 7.9 No Percentage Rent Below Breakpoint.** No Percentage Rent shall be payable for any Rent Year in which Gross Revenues do not exceed the Breakpoint for such Rent Year. Percentage Rent shall not be cumulative, and a shortfall in one Rent Year shall not be carried forward.

**Section 7.10 Relationship to Base Rent.** Percentage Rent is additional rent and is independent of Base Rent. Tenant shall not be entitled to credit Base Rent against Percentage Rent, or Percentage Rent against Base Rent, except pursuant to an Express Offset.

# ARTICLE 8 — TAXES, ASSESSMENTS, AND TAX ABATEMENT

**Section 8.1 Triple-Net Structure.** This Lease is intended to be a triple-net ground lease. Subject to Sections 8.2 and 8.6 through 8.8, Tenant shall pay all Taxes levied or assessed against the Premises and the Improvements during the Term.

**Section 8.2 "Taxes" Defined.** **"Taxes"** means all real property taxes, ad valorem taxes, special assessments, benefit assessments, betterment assessments, sewer and water charges and assessments, and other governmental impositions of every kind levied or assessed upon or with respect to the Premises or the Improvements, together with all costs (including reasonable attorneys' and consultants' fees) reasonably incurred in contesting the same. **"Taxes" shall exclude:**

> (a) franchise, income, inheritance, estate, gift, and transfer taxes of Landlord or Tenant;
>
> (b) any tax, assessment, or charge imposed on Landlord's fee interest measured by Landlord's net income or receipts, other than real property taxes on the Premises;
>
> (c) any tax or charge resulting from Landlord's own act, negligence, or default, or attributable to a period before the Lease Commencement Date or after the expiration of the Term;
>
> (d) any interest or penalty resulting from Landlord's failure to pay or forward a tax bill or assessment timely received by Landlord;
>
> (e) any special assessment for public improvements levied against the Premises that is payable in installments extending beyond the Term, except to the extent attributable to the period during the Term; and
>
> (f) Tenant's personal property taxes, which shall be Tenant's obligation separately.

**Section 8.3 Payment; Contest.** Tenant shall pay Taxes before delinquency. **Tenant shall have the right, at its sole cost and expense and in its own name or in Landlord's name (and Landlord shall cooperate and join in any such proceeding if required), to contest by appropriate legal proceeding the validity or amount of any Taxes.** Landlord shall, within ten (10) Business Days after receipt, deliver to Tenant copies of all tax bills, assessment notices, and notices of valuation received by Landlord. Tenant may defer payment of any contested Tax, provided that Tenant (i) complies with applicable law and any bonding or escrow requirement so that the Premises is not subject to a tax sale or lien enforcement, and (ii) indemnifies Landlord. Any refund received on a contested Tax shall belong to Tenant to the extent Tenant paid the Tax.

**Section 8.4 Proration.** Taxes for the fiscal year in which the Lease Commencement Date occurs shall be prorated as of the Lease Commencement Date. Taxes for the fiscal year in which the Term ends shall be prorated as of the expiration date based on the most recent ascertainable tax bill. Because Tenant is responsible for Taxes for the entire Term (except as provided in Section 8.7), the Parties anticipate no proration other than at the beginning and end of the Term.

**Section 8.5 Landlord Covenants Regarding the Tax Abatement.** **Landlord shall, at its sole cost and expense: (a) use its best efforts to obtain all approvals and authorizations of the City, including any required action of the Port Calloway Board of Finance or the Connecticut Office of Policy and Management, necessary to implement the tax abatement program described in Section 8.6; (b) cause the Tax Abatement Agreement in the form attached as Exhibit L to be executed and delivered by the City and to be in full force and effect no later than the Rent Commencement Date; (c) take all actions necessary to maintain the tax abatement program in effect throughout the Abatement Period; and (d) timely notify Tenant of, and cooperate with Tenant in responding to, any proposed modification, suspension, or revocation of the tax abatement program.**

**Section 8.6 Tax Abatement Program.**

> (a) **Applicable Percentage; Abatement Period.** For each Rent Year during the fifteen (15) year period commencing on the Rent Commencement Date (the **"Abatement Period"**), Tenant's obligation for Taxes on the Premises and the Improvements shall be calculated on the following percentage of the actual assessed value of the Premises and the Improvements (the **"Applicable Percentage"**):
>
> > | Rent Year(s) of Abatement Period | Applicable Percentage |
> > |---|---|
> > | 1 – 5 | 25% |
> > | 6 – 10 | 50% |
> > | 11 – 15 | 75% |
> > | 16 and thereafter | 100% |
>
> (b) **Commencement of Abatement Period.** **The Abatement Period shall commence on the Rent Commencement Date and not on the Lease Commencement Date.** The Parties agree that the tax abatement program was provided to make the Project's operating economics viable during lease-up and stabilization, and that a construction period of up to thirty-six (36) months precedes the Rent Commencement Date.
>
> (c) **Calculation During Construction Period.** From the Lease Commencement Date through the day immediately preceding the Rent Commencement Date, Tenant's obligation for Taxes shall be calculated on one hundred percent (100%) of the actual assessed value of the Premises and the Improvements as assessed from time to time (which the Parties anticipate, prior to completion of the Improvements, to reflect the land value and any partially completed improvements assessed by the City).
>
> (d) **Use of Actual Assessments.** Taxes during and after the Abatement Period shall be calculated by multiplying the actual assessed value of the Premises and the Improvements, as determined by the Port Calloway Tax Assessor, by the actual mill rate then in effect, and then by the Applicable Percentage. **The Parties acknowledge that the projections in the Term Sheet (post-development assessed value of $178,000,000 and mill rate of 34.75 mills, yielding $6,185,500 per annum at full assessment) were estimates only, that the actual assessed value and mill rate will vary over the Term, and that Taxes shall be calculated on the actual assessed value and actual mill rate.**
>
> (e) **Estimated Savings.** For illustration only, the Parties acknowledge that the Term Sheet estimated annual Taxes during the first phase of the abatement at $1,546,375, during the second phase at $3,092,750, during the third phase at $4,639,125, and at full assessment at $6,185,500, in each case based on a projected assessed value of $178,000,000 and a mill rate of 34.75 mills.

**Section 8.7 Failure to Implement or Maintain Abatement.** If, for any reason other than Tenant's own act or omission, the tax abatement program described in Section 8.6 is not implemented as of the Rent Commencement Date, or ceases to be available at any time during the Abatement Period, then:

> (a) **Cap on Tenant's Tax Obligation.** Tenant's obligation for Taxes shall in no event exceed the amount that would have been payable had the tax abatement program been in effect in accordance with Section 8.6;
>
> (b) **Landlord Payment or Offset.** Landlord shall pay to Tenant, within thirty (30) days after written demand, the amount of any Taxes paid by Tenant in excess of the amount determined under clause (a), and Tenant may offset any such amount against Base Rent as an Express Offset;
>
> (c) **Equitable Adjustment of Other Economic Terms.** If the deficiency cannot be cured by Landlord's payment, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith an equitable adjustment to the economic terms of this Lease sufficient to restore the economics the Parties intended, and if they cannot agree within sixty (60) days, the matter shall be resolved in accordance with Article 23; and
>
> (d) **No Event of Default.** Tenant's payment of Taxes in the amount capped by clause (a) shall not constitute an Event of Default, non-payment, or breach of this Lease, notwithstanding any provision of this Lease to the contrary.

**Section 8.8 Change in Tax Regime.** If any Governmental Authority imposes a new or additional tax, assessment, charge, or fee on the Premises, the Improvements, or the leasehold estate that is not a Tax as defined in Section 8.2 during the Term, Tenant shall pay the same (subject to Article 9.2; but Tenant's obligation under this Section 8.8 shall be subject to the following):

> (a) Tenant shall have no obligation to pay any tax that is imposed on Landlord's ownership of the fee interest as distinguished from the occupancy or use of the Premises;

> (b) If a payment in lieu of taxes (PILOT) arrangement, revenue-sharing arrangement, or similar program replaces or supersedes the tax abatement program or the real property tax regime, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith to preserve Tenant's economic position, and Tenant's obligation shall not exceed the amount Tenant would have paid under Section 8.6; and

> (c) Tenant shall have the right, at its cost, to contest any such new imposition in accordance with Section 8.3.

**Section 8.9 Landlord's Tax Obligations; Records.** Landlord shall promptly deliver to Tenant all tax bills, notices of assessment, and valuation notices received by Landlord and shall, upon Tenant's request, provide Tenant with copies of Landlord's records relating to the assessment of the Premises. Landlord shall not contest or appeal any assessed valuation of the Premises without Tenant's prior written consent (which shall not be unreasonably withheld), and Tenant shall have the right to conduct and control any such appeal.

**Section 8.10 Special Assessments.** If any special assessment is levied against the Premises, Tenant may elect to pay it in installments over the longest period permitted and shall be responsible only for installments (including interest) attributable to the period during the Term. At the expiration of the Term, Tenant shall have no obligation with respect to installments not then due.
