> (i) lease termination payments, buy-out payments, and settlement proceeds received from subtenants;
>
> (j) amounts received from any warranty, guaranty, indemnity, or claim;
>
> (k) sales, use, occupancy, hotel, and amusement taxes, and any other taxes or governmental charges collected from subtenants and remitted to a taxing authority;
>
> (l) bad debt recoveries to the extent previously written off and excluded from Gross Revenues;
>
> (m) refunds, rebates, and credits (other than refunds of amounts previously included in Gross Revenues);
>
> (n) employee, guest, and resident concession and discount amounts to the extent not collected;
>
> (o) amounts received from the sale of affordable housing tax credits, low-income housing tax credits, or any similar tax incentive;
>
> (p) grants, subsidies, and incentive payments received from any Governmental Authority; and
>
> (q) any amounts that are not true revenue to Tenant, including amounts collected on behalf of third parties.

**In addition, Gross Revenues shall be determined without including any revenue from a business or activity that is not conducted at the Premises.** Tenant may satisfy its obligations under this Article 7 by delivering a statement of Gross Revenues prepared on the same basis as the Project's audited or reviewed annual financial statements, consistently applied.

**Section 7.4 Deductions from Gross Revenues.** In calculating Gross Revenues, Tenant may deduct (a) amounts actually written off as uncollectible during the Rent Year in accordance with Tenant's customary accounting practices, and (b) the amount of any rent concession, free rent, or abatement actually granted to a subtenant.

**Section 7.5 Indexation of the Breakpoint.** **The Breakpoint shall be adjusted on each Reset Date** by multiplying the Breakpoint in effect immediately prior to such Reset Date by the same fraction used to calculate the CPI-based adjustment to Base Rent under Section 6.5(b) for such Reset Date. **In no event shall the Breakpoint be reduced below $28,500,000.** The Breakpoint as so adjusted shall apply to the Rent Year beginning on the applicable Reset Date and to each Rent Year thereafter until the next Reset Date. Tenant shall deliver to Landlord, together with the statement required by Section 6.10, a statement setting forth the Breakpoint as adjusted.

**The Parties acknowledge that the purpose of this Section 7.5 is to preserve over the full ninety-nine (99) year Term the economic relationship between the Breakpoint and project revenues that the Parties negotiated in 2025, so that Percentage Rent operates as a participation in the Project's real growth rather than as a levy on inflationary revenue increases.**

**Section 7.6 Cumulative Adjustment for Non-Reset Periods [Reserved].**

**Section 7.7 Calculation, Statement, and Payment.** Percentage Rent for each Rent Year shall be calculated annually and shall be due and payable within ninety (90) days after the end of such Rent Year. Each payment shall be accompanied by a certified statement of Gross Revenues for the applicable Rent Year, prepared in accordance with Section 7.2 on a basis consistent with the Project's annual financial statements, and signed by an authorized officer of Tenant. **If Tenant fails to deliver the statement and pay any Percentage Rent when due and such failure continues for thirty (30) days after written notice from Landlord, the unpaid amount shall bear interest in accordance with Section 6.8, but such failure shall not of itself constitute an Event of Default until such thirty (30) day period has expired.**

**Section 7.8 Audit.** Landlord shall have the right, exercisable not more than once in any Rent Year and not more than once with respect to any Rent Year, to audit Tenant's books and records relating to Gross Revenues for the two (2) Rent Years most recently ended, upon not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice. Any such audit shall be conducted by an independent certified public accountant reasonably acceptable to Tenant, during normal business hours, at Tenant's principal place of business or remotely, and in a manner that does not unreasonably interfere with the operation of the Project. **The following shall apply to any audit:**

> (a) **Cost.** If the audit discloses an underpayment of Percentage Rent of five percent (5%) or more for the audited Rent Year, Tenant shall reimburse Landlord for the reasonable out-of-pocket cost of the audit. If the audit discloses an underpayment of less than five percent (5%), or discloses an overpayment, Landlord shall bear the full cost of the audit.
>
> (b) **Payment or Credit.** Any underpayment disclosed by an audit shall be paid by Tenant within thirty (30) days after delivery of the auditor's report, together with interest at the rate set forth in Section 6.8 from the original due date. Any overpayment shall be credited against the next installment of Base Rent or, if no further Rent is payable, refunded within thirty (30) days.
>
> (c) **Records.** Tenant shall maintain complete and accurate books and records relating to Gross Revenues for not less than three (3) years following the end of each Rent Year, and Landlord's audit right with respect to any Rent Year shall expire twenty-four (24) months after the delivery of the statement for such Rent Year.
>
> (d) **Confidentiality.** Landlord shall, and shall cause its auditor to, keep all information obtained in any audit confidential and shall not disclose it except to its Board, its attorneys, its auditors, or as required by the Connecticut Freedom of Information Act or other applicable law. Landlord shall assert all available exemptions, including Conn. Gen. Stat. § 1-210(b)(5) (trade secrets and commercial or financial information), before disclosing any such information.
>
> (e) **No Landlord Audit of Subtenant Records.** Landlord's audit right extends only to Tenant's records, and Landlord shall have no right to audit Tenant's subtenants directly.

**Section 7.9 No Percentage Rent Below Breakpoint.** No Percentage Rent shall be payable for any Rent Year in which Gross Revenues do not exceed the Breakpoint for such Rent Year. Percentage Rent shall not be cumulative, and a shortfall in one Rent Year shall not be carried forward.

**Section 7.10 Relationship to Base Rent.** Percentage Rent is additional rent and is independent of Base Rent. Tenant shall not be entitled to credit Base Rent against Percentage Rent, or Percentage Rent against Base Rent, except pursuant to an Express Offset.

# ARTICLE 8 — TAXES, ASSESSMENTS, AND TAX ABATEMENT

**Section 8.1 Triple-Net Structure.** This Lease is intended to be a triple-net ground lease. Subject to Sections 8.2 and 8.6 through 8.8, Tenant shall pay all Taxes levied or assessed against the Premises and the Improvements during the Term.

**Section 8.2 "Taxes" Defined.** **"Taxes"** means all real property taxes, ad valorem taxes, special assessments, benefit assessments, betterment assessments, sewer and water charges and assessments, and other governmental impositions of every kind levied or assessed upon or with respect to the Premises or the Improvements, together with all costs (including reasonable attorneys' and consultants' fees) reasonably incurred in contesting the same. **"Taxes" shall exclude:**

> (a) franchise, income, inheritance, estate, gift, and transfer taxes of Landlord or Tenant;
>
> (b) any tax, assessment, or charge imposed on Landlord's fee interest measured by Landlord's net income or receipts, other than real property taxes on the Premises;
>
> (c) any tax or charge resulting from Landlord's own act, negligence, or default, or attributable to a period before the Lease Commencement Date or after the expiration of the Term;
>
> (d) any interest or penalty resulting from Landlord's failure to pay or forward a tax bill or assessment timely received by Landlord;
>
> (e) any special assessment for public improvements levied against the Premises that is payable in installments extending beyond the Term, except to the extent attributable to the period during the Term; and
>
> (f) Tenant's personal property taxes, which shall be Tenant's obligation separately.

**Section 8.3 Payment; Contest.** Tenant shall pay Taxes before delinquency. **Tenant shall have the right, at its sole cost and expense and in its own name or in Landlord's name (and Landlord shall cooperate and join in any such proceeding if required), to contest by appropriate legal proceeding the validity or amount of any Taxes.** Landlord shall, within ten (10) Business Days after receipt, deliver to Tenant copies of all tax bills, assessment notices, and notices of valuation received by Landlord. Tenant may defer payment of any contested Tax, provided that Tenant (i) complies with applicable law and any bonding or escrow requirement so that the Premises is not subject to a tax sale or lien enforcement, and (ii) indemnifies Landlord. Any refund received on a contested Tax shall belong to Tenant to the extent Tenant paid the Tax.

**Section 8.4 Proration.** Taxes for the fiscal year in which the Lease Commencement Date occurs shall be prorated as of the Lease Commencement Date. Taxes for the fiscal year in which the Term ends shall be prorated as of the expiration date based on the most recent ascertainable tax bill. Because Tenant is responsible for Taxes for the entire Term (except as provided in Section 8.7), the Parties anticipate no proration other than at the beginning and end of the Term.

**Section 8.5 Landlord Covenants Regarding the Tax Abatement.** **Landlord shall, at its sole cost and expense: (a) use its best efforts to obtain all approvals and authorizations of the City, including any required action of the Port Calloway Board of Finance or the Connecticut Office of Policy and Management, necessary to implement the tax abatement program described in Section 8.6; (b) cause the Tax Abatement Agreement in the form attached as Exhibit L to be executed and delivered by the City and to be in full force and effect no later than the Rent Commencement Date; (c) take all actions necessary to maintain the tax abatement program in effect throughout the Abatement Period; and (d) timely notify Tenant of, and cooperate with Tenant in responding to, any proposed modification, suspension, or revocation of the tax abatement program.**

**Section 8.6 Tax Abatement Program.**

> (a) **Applicable Percentage; Abatement Period.** For each Rent Year during the fifteen (15) year period commencing on the Rent Commencement Date (the **"Abatement Period"**), Tenant's obligation for Taxes on the Premises and the Improvements shall be calculated on the following percentage of the actual assessed value of the Premises and the Improvements (the **"Applicable Percentage"**):
>
> > | Rent Year(s) of Abatement Period | Applicable Percentage |
> > |---|---|
> > | 1 – 5 | 25% |
> > | 6 – 10 | 50% |
> > | 11 – 15 | 75% |
> > | 16 and thereafter | 100% |
>
> (b) **Commencement of Abatement Period.** **The Abatement Period shall commence on the Rent Commencement Date and not on the Lease Commencement Date.** The Parties agree that the tax abatement program was provided to make the Project's operating economics viable during lease-up and stabilization, and that a construction period of up to thirty-six (36) months precedes the Rent Commencement Date.
>
> (c) **Calculation During Construction Period.** From the Lease Commencement Date through the day immediately preceding the Rent Commencement Date, Tenant's obligation for Taxes shall be calculated on one hundred percent (100%) of the actual assessed value of the Premises and the Improvements as assessed from time to time (which the Parties anticipate, prior to completion of the Improvements, to reflect the land value and any partially completed improvements assessed by the City).
>
> (d) **Use of Actual Assessments.** Taxes during and after the Abatement Period shall be calculated by multiplying the actual assessed value of the Premises and the Improvements, as determined by the Port Calloway Tax Assessor, by the actual mill rate then in effect, and then by the Applicable Percentage. **The Parties acknowledge that the projections in the Term Sheet (post-development assessed value of $178,000,000 and mill rate of 34.75 mills, yielding $6,185,500 per annum at full assessment) were estimates only, that the actual assessed value and mill rate will vary over the Term, and that Taxes shall be calculated on the actual assessed value and actual mill rate.**
>
> (e) **Estimated Savings.** For illustration only, the Parties acknowledge that the Term Sheet estimated annual Taxes during the first phase of the abatement at $1,546,375, during the second phase at $3,092,750, during the third phase at $4,639,125, and at full assessment at $6,185,500, in each case based on a projected assessed value of $178,000,000 and a mill rate of 34.75 mills.

**Section 8.7 Failure to Implement or Maintain Abatement.** If, for any reason other than Tenant's own act or omission, the tax abatement program described in Section 8.6 is not implemented as of the Rent Commencement Date, or ceases to be available at any time during the Abatement Period, then:

> (a) **Cap on Tenant's Tax Obligation.** Tenant's obligation for Taxes shall in no event exceed the amount that would have been payable had the tax abatement program been in effect in accordance with Section 8.6;
>
> (b) **Landlord Payment or Offset.** Landlord shall pay to Tenant, within thirty (30) days after written demand, the amount of any Taxes paid by Tenant in excess of the amount determined under clause (a), and Tenant may offset any such amount against Base Rent as an Express Offset;
>
> (c) **Equitable Adjustment of Other Economic Terms.** If the deficiency cannot be cured by Landlord's payment, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith an equitable adjustment to the economic terms of this Lease sufficient to restore the economics the Parties intended, and if they cannot agree within sixty (60) days, the matter shall be resolved in accordance with Article 23; and
>
> (d) **No Event of Default.** Tenant's payment of Taxes in the amount capped by clause (a) shall not constitute an Event of Default, non-payment, or breach of this Lease, notwithstanding any provision of this Lease to the contrary.

**Section 8.8 Change in Tax Regime.** If any Governmental Authority imposes a new or additional tax, assessment, charge, or fee on the Premises, the Improvements, or the leasehold estate that is not a Tax as defined in Section 8.2 during the Term, Tenant shall pay the same (subject to Article 9.2; but Tenant's obligation under this Section 8.8 shall be subject to the following):

> (a) Tenant shall have no obligation to pay any tax that is imposed on Landlord's ownership of the fee interest as distinguished from the occupancy or use of the Premises;

> (b) If a payment in lieu of taxes (PILOT) arrangement, revenue-sharing arrangement, or similar program replaces or supersedes the tax abatement program or the real property tax regime, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith to preserve Tenant's economic position, and Tenant's obligation shall not exceed the amount Tenant would have paid under Section 8.6; and

> (c) Tenant shall have the right, at its cost, to contest any such new imposition in accordance with Section 8.3.

**Section 8.9 Landlord's Tax Obligations; Records.** Landlord shall promptly deliver to Tenant all tax bills, notices of assessment, and valuation notices received by Landlord and shall, upon Tenant's request, provide Tenant with copies of Landlord's records relating to the assessment of the Premises. Landlord shall not contest or appeal any assessed valuation of the Premises without Tenant's prior written consent (which shall not be unreasonably withheld), and Tenant shall have the right to conduct and control any such appeal.

**Section 8.10 Special Assessments.** If any special assessment is levied against the Premises, Tenant may elect to pay it in installments over the longest period permitted and shall be responsible only for installments (including interest) attributable to the period during the Term. At the expiration of the Term, Tenant shall have no obligation with respect to installments not then due.

# ARTICLE 9 — ENVIRONMENTAL MATTERS

**Section 9.1 Landlord's Environmental Representations and Warranties.** Landlord represents and warrants to Tenant as of the Effective Date and as of the Lease Commencement Date that, except as disclosed in the Phase I Environmental Site Assessment dated March 15, 2025 (Report No. HEC-2025-0318), the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment dated May 2, 2025 (Report No. HEC-2025-0412), the ELUR, and the reports referenced in the title commitment:

> (a) Landlord has delivered to Tenant true and complete copies of all environmental reports, assessments, sampling data, regulatory correspondence, and DEEP files in Landlord's possession or control relating to the Premises;

> (b) there is no Release of Hazardous Materials at, on, under, or migrating from the Premises other than the contamination described in the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment as Area 1 (approximately 4,200 square feet in the northwest corner) and Area 2 (approximately 1,600 square feet in the former dry dock area);

> (c) Landlord has received no written notice from any Governmental Authority of any violation of Environmental Laws, any Release, or any enforcement action relating to the Premises that remains unresolved;

> (d) the ELUR has not been violated by Landlord and remains in full force and effect;

> (e) Landlord has made all filings, and given all notices, required under Environmental Laws with respect to the conditions existing as of the Lease Commencement Date, including all filings relating to the removal of the underground storage tanks formerly located in the northwest corner of the Premises; and

> (f) the estimate of $2,400,000 for the Remediation (comprising $1,850,000 for Area 1 and $550,000 for Area 2) was prepared by Halcyon Environmental Consultants Inc. as an opinion-level estimate on the basis described in the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment, and Landlord is not aware of any condition at the Premises that would cause the actual cost of the Tenant Remediation Scope to exceed such estimate.

**Section 9.2 Landlord's Environmental Covenants.** Landlord covenants that it shall: (a) not cause or permit any Release of Hazardous Materials at the Premises; (b) maintain the ELUR in full force and effect and take no action to modify or release it in a manner that adversely affects the Project; (c) perform all obligations of the "owner" under the ELUR that are not allocated to Tenant under this Lease; (d) cooperate fully, at Landlord's cost as to matters arising from pre-existing conditions, in obtaining any ELUR modification, variance, interpretation, or release from DEEP that is necessary for the Project; and (e) discharge any lien filed against the Premises under Conn. Gen. Stat. § 22a-119a or any comparable Environmental Law arising from conditions existing as of the Lease Commencement Date, or from any act of Landlord.

**Section 9.3 ELUR Compliance; Ground-Floor Use.**

> (a) The Parties acknowledge that the ELUR prohibits residential use on the ground floor of any structure on the Premises, defining "residential use" as habitable space at or below finished grade elevation intended for residential dwelling, sleeping, cooking, or eating, and that the ELUR does not expressly address non-habitable ancillary spaces serving a residential building, such as lobbies, mail rooms, fitness centers, package rooms, resident lounges, and leasing offices. **The Parties further acknowledge that the proposed Project contemplates a ground-floor residential lobby and amenity spaces, and that the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment recommends that Tenant obtain a formal interpretation or variance from DEEP clarifying the permissibility of such spaces.**

> (b) **Landlord Obligation.** **Landlord shall, at its sole cost and expense and as a condition to the Lease Commencement Date, obtain from DEEP a written interpretation, variance, or modification of the ELUR confirming that ground-floor residential lobby, amenity, leasing, and management spaces (as distinct from dwelling units) are permitted under the ELUR, or, if such confirmation is not obtained, an amendment to the ELUR permitting such uses.** Landlord shall diligently pursue such confirmation and shall keep Tenant reasonably informed. Tenant shall cooperate with Landlord's efforts and shall furnish such design and technical information as Landlord reasonably requires.

> (c) **Interim Protection.** Pending receipt of the confirmation described in Section 9.3(b), Tenant may proceed with the Project using a ground-floor program that Tenant reasonably determines to be consistent with the ELUR (including by locating dwelling units on floors 2 and above and limiting ground-floor uses to retail, commercial, mechanical, parking, and other clearly non-habitable functions), and no such design decision shall constitute a breach of this Lease.

> (d) **DEEP Enforcement.** If DEEP asserts that any portion of the Project as designed violates the ELUR, and such assertion results from the ELUR's ambiguity rather than from Tenant's deviation from the approved plans or Tenant's failure to comply with Section 9.3, then (i) Landlord shall bear the cost of any required design modification, abatement, penalty, or remedial action, and (ii) the applicable Development Milestone deadlines shall be extended by the period of delay in accordance with Section 4.4(a). Landlord shall indemnify Tenant for any fine, penalty, or cost arising from such assertion, except to the extent caused by Tenant's negligence or willful misconduct.

> (e) **Affordable Units Placement.** Tenant shall locate all affordable housing units on floors above the ground floor, consistent with the ELUR and the recommendations in the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment, and the Affordable Housing Regulatory Agreement shall so provide.

**Section 9.4 Environmental Remediation — Allocation of Responsibility.**

> (a) **Tenant Remediation Scope.** Tenant shall perform, at its cost subject to the Remediation Credit, the investigation, excavation, off-site disposal, backfill, confirmation sampling, and reporting necessary to address the contamination identified in the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment within Area 1 (approximately 4,200 square feet) and Area 2 (approximately 1,600 square feet), substantially in accordance with the scope and budget described in **Exhibit H** and the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment, all in compliance with the RSRs, the ELUR, and a DEEP-approved Remedial Action Plan and Soil Management Plan (collectively, the **"Tenant Remediation Scope"**).

> (b) **Landlord Responsibility.** **Landlord shall be solely responsible, at its sole cost and expense and without reimbursement from Tenant, for: (i) all environmental conditions at the Premises existing as of the Lease Commencement Date that are not within the Tenant Remediation Scope; (ii) all costs of investigating, remediating, monitoring, and closing out the former underground storage tank locations and any DEEP Leaking Underground Storage Tank file or "closure pending/incomplete" status; (iii) all costs of obtaining any ELUR modification or release required by Section 9.3; (iv) all costs of addressing any Release that migrates off-site or any off-site impact from pre-existing conditions; (v) all costs of addressing any contamination discovered during construction outside the areas delineated in the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment; and (vi) all costs arising from any third-party claim, natural resource damage claim, or governmental enforcement action relating to conditions existing as of the Lease Commencement Date.**

> (c) **Cap on Tenant's Environmental Liability.** **Tenant's aggregate liability for the cost of the Tenant Remediation Scope shall not exceed Six Hundred Thousand Dollars ($600,000). Any actual cost of the Tenant Remediation Scope in excess of $2,400,000 in the aggregate shall be borne by Landlord.** If the aggregate cost of the Tenant Remediation Scope is less than $2,400,000, the Remediation Credit shall not be reduced or adjusted, and Tenant shall retain the benefit of the Remediation Credit in the full amount of $1,800,000.

> (d) **Landlord Indemnity for Pre-Existing Conditions.** **Landlord shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Tenant, its members, its Leasehold Mortgagee, and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, and affiliates from and against all claims, liabilities, losses, damages, penalties, fines, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' and consultants' fees, and including response costs and natural resource damages) arising out of or relating to (i) any Release or condition of Hazardous Materials at, on, under, or migrating from the Premises existing as of the Lease Commencement Date, (ii) Landlord's breach of Section 9.1 or 9.2, (iii) any off-site migration of pre-existing contamination, and (iv) any claim by a third party relating to pre-existing conditions, in each case regardless of whether the claim is asserted during or after the Term.**

> (e) **Tenant Indemnity.** Tenant shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Landlord from and against all claims, liabilities, losses, damages, penalties, fines, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) arising out of or relating to any Release of Hazardous Materials at the Premises caused by Tenant's acts or omissions after the Lease Commencement Date, other than a Release of pre-existing contamination caused by Tenant's properly conducted construction activities in compliance with the approved Remedial Action Plan and Soil Management Plan, and other than matters for which Landlord is responsible under Section 9.4(b).

> (f) **Survival.** The indemnities in Sections 9.4(d) and 9.4(e) shall survive the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease.

**Section 9.5 Remediation Credit.**

> (a) **Amount.** Landlord shall provide to Tenant a credit against Base Rent in the aggregate amount of **One Million Eight Hundred Thousand Dollars ($1,800,000)** (the **"Remediation Credit"**), without interest, in consideration of Tenant's assumption of the Tenant Remediation Scope.

> (b) **Application.** The Remediation Credit shall be applied against the monthly installments of Base Rent first coming due after the Rent Commencement Date, as follows: (i) the monthly Base Rent installments for the first seven (7) full calendar months after the Rent Commencement Date shall be reduced to $0 (7 × $237,500 = $1,662,500); (ii) the monthly Base Rent installment for the eighth (8th) full calendar month after the Rent Commencement Date shall be reduced by $137,500 (so that Tenant pays $100,000 for such month); and (iii) commencing with the ninth (9th) full calendar month after the Rent Commencement Date, the full monthly Base Rent shall be payable.

> (c) **Carryforward.** If Base Rent for any month is not payable in full (whether by reason of Casualty, Condemnation, Express Offset, or otherwise), the unapplied portion of the Remediation Credit shall be carried forward to the next month in which Base Rent is payable, and shall not be forfeited.

> (d) **Cash Payment on Early Termination.** **If this Lease expires or is terminated before the Remediation Credit has been applied in full, Landlord shall pay to Tenant, in cash, within thirty (30) days after the effective date of such expiration or termination, the unapplied balance of the Remediation Credit.**

> (e) **No Condition on Credit.** The Remediation Credit is not conditioned on the actual cost of the Tenant Remediation Scope, on the timing of the Remediation, or on Tenant's completion of the Remediation, except that Landlord's obligation to apply the Remediation Credit is subject to Tenant not being in an uncured monetary Event of Default.

> (f) **Documentation.** Tenant shall deliver to Landlord, within thirty (30) days after completion of the Tenant Remediation Scope, a certificate of a LEP describing the work performed and the costs incurred. Landlord shall have the right to review such certificate, but shall have no right to audit Tenant's costs or to reduce the Remediation Credit on the basis of such review.

**Section 9.6 Remediation Standards and Approvals.**

> (a) Tenant shall engage a LEP to oversee and certify completion of the Tenant Remediation Scope, and shall cause the Remediation to be performed in compliance with the RSRs, the ELUR, a DEEP-approved Remedial Action Plan, and a DEEP-approved Soil Management Plan.

> (b) **Landlord Cooperation.** Landlord shall cooperate with Tenant, at Tenant's cost except where the approval is required because of the ELUR's ambiguity or Landlord's acts, in obtaining all DEEP approvals, including any ELUR modification required by Section 9.3.

> (c) **Engineered Barrier.** Tenant shall maintain, inspect, and repair the engineered barrier required by the ELUR in accordance with the ELUR's requirements, provided that the cost of reconstructing or repairing the engineered barrier to the extent it was deficient or improperly installed as of the Lease Commencement Date shall be borne by Landlord.

> (d) **Delays.** Any delay in obtaining DEEP approvals shall constitute an extension of the Development Milestones in accordance with Section 4.4(a) and shall not constitute an Event of Default.

**Section 9.7 Ongoing Environmental Compliance.** Following completion of the Tenant Remediation Scope, Tenant shall be responsible for the ongoing environmental compliance obligations applicable to the Premises arising after the Lease Commencement Date, including (a) maintenance, inspection, and repair of the engineered barrier; (b) annual compliance certifications to DEEP; (c) groundwater monitoring required by any DEEP-approved plan; (d) the prohibition on installation of potable water wells; and (e) compliance with all Environmental Laws applicable to the operation of the Project. Landlord shall timely deliver to Tenant any notices, correspondence, or orders received from DEEP or any other Governmental Authority relating to the Premises.

**Section 9.8 Transfer Act and Regulatory Filings.** The Parties shall cooperate to determine whether this Lease, the commencement of construction, or the commencement of operations constitutes a "transfer of establishment" or otherwise triggers any filing obligation under the Connecticut Transfer Act (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 22a-134 *et seq.*) or any similar Environmental Law. **Landlord shall be responsible, at its sole cost and expense, for the preparation and filing of any Form I, II, III, or IV, or any successor form, required as a result of the transfer of the Premises to Tenant or the conditions existing at the Premises as of the Lease Commencement Date, and for any investigation, remediation, or verification required to obtain DEEP's approval of the same.** Tenant shall provide such information regarding its intended use of the Premises as Landlord reasonably requires. Landlord shall indemnify Tenant for any liability arising from any failure to make a required filing or to perform required investigation or remediation relating to pre-existing conditions.

**Section 9.9 Environmental Insurance.** Tenant shall maintain the environmental liability insurance required by Section 14.2(f). **The Parties acknowledge that pollution legal liability insurance may exclude known conditions, and that Tenant's inability to obtain coverage for the known conditions described in the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment shall not constitute a breach of this Lease so long as Tenant maintains the coverage required by Section 14.2(f) to the extent commercially available.** Landlord shall not be entitled to require Tenant to obtain coverage for pre-existing conditions.

**Section 9.10 No Assumption; Tenant Not an Owner or Operator of Pre-Existing Conditions.** Nothing in this Lease shall be construed to make Tenant the owner or operator of the Premises for purposes of Environmental Laws with respect to conditions existing as of the Lease Commencement Date, and Landlord acknowledges that Tenant's leasehold interest does not transfer to Tenant any liability for such conditions except as expressly provided in Section 9.4(a).

# ARTICLE 10 — SECURITY DEPOSIT

**Section 10.1 Form and Amount.** On or before the Lease Commencement Date, Tenant shall deliver to Landlord a security deposit in the amount of **Five Million Seven Hundred Thousand Dollars ($5,700,000)**, equal to twenty-four (24) months of the initial monthly Base Rent, in the form of (a) an irrevocable standby letter of credit in the form attached as Exhibit J, issued by a commercial bank organized under the laws of the United States or any state thereof having a minimum credit rating of A- from Standard & Poor's or A3 from Moody's Investors Service (or an equivalent rating from a nationally recognized rating agency) and naming Landlord as beneficiary (the **"LOC"**), or (b) at Tenant's election, a cash deposit in such amount, held in an interest-bearing escrow account for the benefit of Landlord and Tenant (the **"Cash Deposit"**). The LOC and the Cash Deposit are referred to collectively as the **"Security Deposit."**

**Section 10.2 Reduction.** **The Security Deposit shall be reduced to Two Million Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars ($2,850,000), equal to twelve (12) months of the initial monthly Base Rent, upon Tenant's satisfaction of the Reduction Conditions.** The **"Reduction Conditions"** are satisfied when:

> (a) the Project has achieved and maintained an overall occupancy rate of ninety percent (90%) or greater for twenty-four (24) consecutive months, measured as of the last day of each calendar month during such period;

> (b) Tenant has delivered to Landlord a certificate of the Managing Member of Tenant certifying the occupancy rate for each month in such period, together with supporting rent roll data for each such month; and

> (c) no Event of Default by Tenant has occurred and is continuing.

**Section 10.3 Measurement of Occupancy.** For purposes of Section 10.2, **"occupancy rate"** means the ratio, expressed as a percentage, of (a) the aggregate net rentable square footage of the residential units, office space, and retail space within the Project that is subject to a lease or occupancy agreement under which the occupant has taken possession and is obligated to pay rent (excluding any space occupied by Tenant or its Affiliates and excluding any space subject to a lease that is in default beyond applicable notice and cure periods), to (b) the aggregate net rentable square footage of all residential units, office space, and retail space within the Project that is then available for occupancy. Tenant shall determine the rentable square footage in accordance with the measurement standard used in the Project's leases, consistently applied, and shall furnish the calculation to Landlord with its certificate.

**Section 10.4 Reduction Mechanics and Timeline.** Within thirty (30) days after Landlord's receipt of the certificate and supporting data described in Section 10.2(b), Landlord shall deliver to Tenant either (a) a written acknowledgment that the Reduction Conditions have been satisfied, or (b) a written objection stating with specificity the basis for the objection. **If Landlord fails to deliver a written objection within such thirty (30) day period, the Reduction Conditions shall be deemed satisfied.** If Landlord delivers a timely objection, the Parties shall confer in good faith for thirty (30) days, after which either Party may submit the dispute to resolution under Article 23. Upon satisfaction or deemed satisfaction of the Reduction Conditions, Tenant shall deliver (i) a replacement LOC in the reduced amount, or (ii) if a Cash Deposit is held, Landlord shall return the excess amount to Tenant, in each case within ten (10) Business Days. **Landlord's failure to return or exchange the Security Deposit within such period shall entitle Tenant to offset the excess amount against Base Rent.**

**Section 10.5 Draws.** Landlord may draw upon the Security Deposit only upon the occurrence of an uncured monetary Event of Default by Tenant, and only in the amount of the sums then due and unpaid (including interest and Landlord's reasonable costs of enforcement). **Landlord shall have no right to draw upon the Security Deposit (a) on account of a non-monetary Event of Default, (b) on account of a Milestone failure except as limited by Section 5.8, (c) in anticipation of a default, or (d) in an amount exceeding its actual damages.** Any amounts drawn shall be applied to Tenant's outstanding obligations under this Lease. Landlord shall give Tenant and each Leasehold Mortgagee written notice of any draw within two (2) Business Days thereafter.

**Section 10.6 Replenishment.** Within thirty (30) days after any draw by Landlord, Tenant shall replenish the Security Deposit to the required amount (as then reduced pursuant to Section 10.2). If Landlord's draw is determined to have been improper, Landlord shall return the amount drawn with interest at the rate set forth in Section 6.8 within ten (10) Business Days after such determination.

**Section 10.7 Renewal; Evergreen.** If the LOC has a stated expiration date, Tenant shall deliver a replacement or renewal LOC not later than thirty (30) days prior to its expiration. Failure to timely deliver a replacement or renewal LOC shall constitute an Event of Default only if such failure continues for fifteen (15) days after written notice from Landlord. Tenant may satisfy this obligation with an evergreen LOC acceptable to Landlord.

**Section 10.8 Return of Security Deposit.** Within thirty (30) days after the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease and the surrender of the Premises in the condition required by Article 20, Landlord shall return the Security Deposit to Tenant (or, at Tenant's election, to the Leasehold Mortgagee), less any amount properly applied in accordance with Section 10.5. **Upon a Reverter Termination, the Security Deposit shall be applied as provided in Section 5.8.**

**Section 10.9 No Landlord Lien.** **Landlord waives any landlord's lien, statutory or otherwise, on Tenant's Trade Fixtures, personal property, subleases, rents, accounts, and other assets of Tenant, and Landlord subordinates any such lien to the Leasehold Mortgage.** Tenant's property shall not be subject to distress, distraint, or execution by Landlord.

# ARTICLE 9 — ENVIRONMENTAL MATTERS

**Section 9.1 Landlord's Environmental Representations and Warranties.** Landlord represents and warrants to Tenant as of the Effective Date and as of the Lease Commencement Date that, except as disclosed in the Phase I Environmental Site Assessment dated March 15, 2025 (Report No. HEC-2025-0318), the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment dated May 2, 2025 (Report No. HEC-2025-0412), the ELUR, and the reports referenced in the title commitment:

> (a) Landlord has delivered to Tenant true and complete copies of all environmental reports, assessments, sampling data, regulatory correspondence, and DEEP files in Landlord's possession or control relating to the Premises;

> (b) there is no Release of Hazardous Materials at, on, under, or migrating from the Premises other than the contamination described in the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment as Area 1 (approximately 4,200 square feet in the northwest corner) and Area 2 (approximately 1,600 square feet in the former dry dock area);

> (c) Landlord has received no written notice from any Governmental Authority of any violation of Environmental Laws, any Release, or any enforcement action relating to the Premises that remains unresolved;

> (d) the ELUR has not been violated by Landlord and remains in full force and effect;

> (e) Landlord has made all filings, and given all notices, required under Environmental Laws with respect to the conditions existing as of the Lease Commencement Date, including all filings relating to the removal of the underground storage tanks formerly located in the northwest corner of the Premises; and

> (f) the estimate of $2,400,000 for the Remediation (comprising $1,850,000 for Area 1 and $550,000 for Area 2) was prepared by Halcyon Environmental Consultants Inc. as an opinion-level estimate on the basis described in the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment, and Landlord is not aware of any condition at the Premises that would cause the actual cost of the Tenant Remediation Scope to exceed such estimate.

**Section 9.2 Landlord's Environmental Covenants.** Landlord covenants that it shall: (a) not cause or permit any Release of Hazardous Materials at the Premises; (b) maintain the ELUR in full force and effect and take no action to modify or release it in a manner that adversely affects the Project; (c) perform all obligations of the "owner" under the ELUR that are not allocated to Tenant under this Lease; (d) cooperate fully, at Landlord's cost as to matters arising from pre-existing conditions, in obtaining any ELUR modification, variance, interpretation, or release from DEEP that is necessary for the Project; and (e) discharge any lien filed against the Premises under Conn. Gen. Stat. § 22a-119a or any comparable Environmental Law arising from conditions existing as of the Lease Commencement Date, or from any act of Landlord.

**Section 9.3 ELUR Compliance; Ground-Floor Use.**

> (a) The Parties acknowledge that the ELUR prohibits residential use on the ground floor of any structure on the Premises, defining "residential use" as habitable space at or below finished grade elevation intended for residential dwelling, sleeping, cooking, or eating, and that the ELUR does not expressly address non-habitable ancillary spaces serving a residential building, such as lobbies, mail rooms, fitness centers, package rooms, resident lounges, and leasing offices. **The Parties further acknowledge that the proposed Project contemplates a ground-floor residential lobby and amenity spaces, and that the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment recommends that Tenant obtain a formal interpretation or variance from DEEP clarifying the permissibility of such spaces.**

> (b) **Landlord Obligation.** **Landlord shall, at its sole cost and expense and as a condition to the Lease Commencement Date, obtain from DEEP a written interpretation, variance, or modification of the ELUR confirming that ground-floor residential lobby, amenity, leasing, and management spaces (as distinct from dwelling units) are permitted under the ELUR, or, if such confirmation is not obtained, an amendment to the ELUR permitting such uses.** Landlord shall diligently pursue such confirmation and shall keep Tenant reasonably informed. Tenant shall cooperate with Landlord's efforts and shall furnish such design and technical information as Landlord reasonably requires.

> (c) **Interim Protection.** Pending receipt of the confirmation described in Section 9.3(b), Tenant may proceed with the Project using a ground-floor program that Tenant reasonably determines to be consistent with the ELUR (including by locating dwelling units on floors 2 and above and limiting ground-floor uses to retail, commercial, mechanical, parking, and other clearly non-habitable functions), and no such design decision shall constitute a breach of this Lease.

> (d) **DEEP Enforcement.** If DEEP asserts that any portion of the Project as designed violates the ELUR, and such assertion results from the ELUR's ambiguity rather than from Tenant's deviation from the approved plans or Tenant's failure to comply with Section 9.3, then (i) Landlord shall bear the cost of any required design modification, abatement, penalty, or remedial action, and (ii) the applicable Development Milestone deadlines shall be extended by the period of delay in accordance with Section 4.4(a). Landlord shall indemnify Tenant for any fine, penalty, or cost arising from such assertion, except to the extent caused by Tenant's negligence or willful misconduct.

> (e) **Affordable Units Placement.** Tenant shall locate all affordable housing units on floors above the ground floor, consistent with the ELUR and the recommendations in the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment, and the Affordable Housing Regulatory Agreement shall so provide.

**Section 9.4 Environmental Remediation — Allocation of Responsibility.**

> (a) **Tenant Remediation Scope.** Tenant shall perform, at its cost subject to the Remediation Credit, the investigation, excavation, off-site disposal, backfill, confirmation sampling, and reporting necessary to address the contamination identified in the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment within Area 1 (approximately 4,200 square feet) and Area 2 (approximately 1,600 square feet), substantially in accordance with the scope and budget described in **Exhibit H** and the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment, all in compliance with the RSRs, the ELUR, and a DEEP-approved Remedial Action Plan and Soil Management Plan (collectively, the **"Tenant Remediation Scope"**).

> (b) **Landlord Responsibility.** **Landlord shall be solely responsible, at its sole cost and expense and without reimbursement from Tenant, for: (i) all environmental conditions at the Premises existing as of the Lease Commencement Date that are not within the Tenant Remediation Scope; (ii) all costs of investigating, remediating, monitoring, and closing out the former underground storage tank locations and any DEEP Leaking Underground Storage Tank file or "closure pending/incomplete" status; (iii) all costs of obtaining any ELUR modification or release required by Section 9.3; (iv) all costs of addressing any Release that migrates off-site or any off-site impact from pre-existing conditions; (v) all costs of addressing any contamination discovered during construction outside the areas delineated in the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment; and (vi) all costs arising from any third-party claim, natural resource damage claim, or governmental enforcement action relating to conditions existing as of the Lease Commencement Date.**

> (c) **Cap on Tenant's Environmental Liability.** **Tenant's aggregate liability for the cost of the Tenant Remediation Scope shall not exceed Six Hundred Thousand Dollars ($600,000). Any actual cost of the Tenant Remediation Scope in excess of $2,400,000 in the aggregate shall be borne by Landlord.** If the aggregate cost of the Tenant Remediation Scope is less than $2,400,000, the Remediation Credit shall not be reduced or adjusted, and Tenant shall retain the benefit of the Remediation Credit in the full amount of $1,800,000.

> (d) **Landlord Indemnity for Pre-Existing Conditions.** **Landlord shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Tenant, its members, its Leasehold Mortgagee, and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, and affiliates from and against all claims, liabilities, losses, damages, penalties, fines, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' and consultants' fees, and including response costs and natural resource damages) arising out of or relating to (i) any Release or condition of Hazardous Materials at, on, under, or migrating from the Premises existing as of the Lease Commencement Date, (ii) Landlord's breach of Section 9.1 or 9.2, (iii) any off-site migration of pre-existing contamination, and (iv) any claim by a third party relating to pre-existing conditions, in each case regardless of whether the claim is asserted during or after the Term.**

> (e) **Tenant Indemnity.** Tenant shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Landlord from and against all claims, liabilities, losses, damages, penalties, fines, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) arising out of or relating to any Release of Hazardous Materials at the Premises caused by Tenant's acts or omissions after the Lease Commencement Date, other than a Release of pre-existing contamination caused by Tenant's properly conducted construction activities in compliance with the approved Remedial Action Plan and Soil Management Plan, and other than matters for which Landlord is responsible under Section 9.4(b).

> (f) **Survival.** The indemnities in Sections 9.4(d) and 9.4(e) shall survive the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease.

**Section 9.5 Remediation Credit.**

> (a) **Amount.** Landlord shall provide to Tenant a credit against Base Rent in the aggregate amount of **One Million Eight Hundred Thousand Dollars ($1,800,000)** (the **"Remediation Credit"**), without interest, in consideration of Tenant's assumption of the Tenant Remediation Scope.

> (b) **Application.** The Remediation Credit shall be applied against the monthly installments of Base Rent first coming due after the Rent Commencement Date, as follows: (i) the monthly Base Rent installments for the first seven (7) full calendar months after the Rent Commencement Date shall be reduced to $0 (7 × $237,500 = $1,662,500); (ii) the monthly Base Rent installment for the eighth (8th) full calendar month after the Rent Commencement Date shall be reduced by $137,500 (so that Tenant pays $100,000 for such month); and (iii) commencing with the ninth (9th) full calendar month after the Rent Commencement Date, the full monthly Base Rent shall be payable.

> (c) **Carryforward.** If Base Rent for any month is not payable in full (whether by reason of Casualty, Condemnation, Express Offset, or otherwise), the unapplied portion of the Remediation Credit shall be carried forward to the next month in which Base Rent is payable, and shall not be forfeited.

> (d) **Cash Payment on Early Termination.** **If this Lease expires or is terminated before the Remediation Credit has been applied in full, Landlord shall pay to Tenant, in cash, within thirty (30) days after the effective date of such expiration or termination, the unapplied balance of the Remediation Credit.**

> (e) **No Condition on Credit.** The Remediation Credit is not conditioned on the actual cost of the Tenant Remediation Scope, on the timing of the Remediation, or on Tenant's completion of the Remediation, except that Landlord's obligation to apply the Remediation Credit is subject to Tenant not being in an uncured monetary Event of Default.

> (f) **Documentation.** Tenant shall deliver to Landlord, within thirty (30) days after completion of the Tenant Remediation Scope, a certificate of a LEP describing the work performed and the costs incurred. Landlord shall have the right to review such certificate, but shall have no right to audit Tenant's costs or to reduce the Remediation Credit on the basis of such review.

**Section 9.6 Remediation Standards and Approvals.**

> (a) Tenant shall engage a LEP to oversee and certify completion of the Tenant Remediation Scope, and shall cause the Remediation to be performed in compliance with the RSRs, the ELUR, a DEEP-approved Remedial Action Plan, and a DEEP-approved Soil Management Plan.

> (b) **Landlord Cooperation.** Landlord shall cooperate with Tenant, at Tenant's cost except where the approval is required because of the ELUR's ambiguity or Landlord's acts, in obtaining all DEEP approvals, including any ELUR modification required by Section 9.3.

> (c) **Engineered Barrier.** Tenant shall maintain, inspect, and repair the engineered barrier required by the ELUR in accordance with the ELUR's requirements, provided that the cost of reconstructing or repairing the engineered barrier to the extent it was deficient or improperly installed as of the Lease Commencement Date shall be borne by Landlord.

> (d) **Delays.** Any delay in obtaining DEEP approvals shall constitute an extension of the Development Milestones in accordance with Section 4.4(a) and shall not constitute an Event of Default.

**Section 9.7 Ongoing Environmental Compliance.** Following completion of the Tenant Remediation Scope, Tenant shall be responsible for the ongoing environmental compliance obligations applicable to the Premises arising after the Lease Commencement Date, including (a) maintenance, inspection, and repair of the engineered barrier; (b) annual compliance certifications to DEEP; (c) groundwater monitoring required by any DEEP-approved plan; (d) the prohibition on installation of potable water wells; and (e) compliance with all Environmental Laws applicable to the operation of the Project. Landlord shall timely deliver to Tenant any notices, correspondence, or orders received from DEEP or any other Governmental Authority relating to the Premises.

**Section 9.8 Transfer Act and Regulatory Filings.** The Parties shall cooperate to determine whether this Lease, the commencement of construction, or the commencement of operations constitutes a "transfer of establishment" or otherwise triggers any filing obligation under the Connecticut Transfer Act (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 22a-134 *et seq.*) or any similar Environmental Law. **Landlord shall be responsible, at its sole cost and expense, for the preparation and filing of any Form I, II, III, or IV, or any successor form, required as a result of the transfer of the Premises to Tenant or the conditions existing at the Premises as of the Lease Commencement Date, and for any investigation, remediation, or verification required to obtain DEEP's approval of the same.** Tenant shall provide such information regarding its intended use of the Premises as Landlord reasonably requires. Landlord shall indemnify Tenant for any liability arising from any failure to make a required filing or to perform required investigation or remediation relating to pre-existing conditions.

**Section 9.9 Environmental Insurance.** Tenant shall maintain the environmental liability insurance required by Section 14.2(f). **The Parties acknowledge that pollution legal liability insurance may exclude known conditions, and that Tenant's inability to obtain coverage for the known conditions described in the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment shall not constitute a breach of this Lease so long as Tenant maintains the coverage required by Section 14.2(f) to the extent commercially available.** Landlord shall not be entitled to require Tenant to obtain coverage for pre-existing conditions.

**Section 9.10 No Assumption; Tenant Not an Owner or Operator of Pre-Existing Conditions.** Nothing in this Lease shall be construed to make Tenant the owner or operator of the Premises for purposes of Environmental Laws with respect to conditions existing as of the Lease Commencement Date, and Landlord acknowledges that Tenant's leasehold interest does not transfer to Tenant any liability for such conditions except as expressly provided in Section 9.4(a).

# ARTICLE 11 — USE, OPERATIONS, AND AFFORDABLE HOUSING

**Section 11.1 Permitted Uses.** Tenant may use the Premises for the following purposes and for no other purpose (the **"Permitted Uses"**): residential apartments (for rent only, subject to Section 11.6), Class A office, ground-floor retail, restaurants (including restaurants with liquor service duly licensed by the Connecticut Department of Consumer Protection), accessory parking, and ancillary amenity, management, leasing, mechanical, utility, and open space uses customary to a mixed-use development. **The following uses are expressly prohibited:** adult entertainment establishments, firearms sales, pawnshops, gasoline service stations, industrial, manufacturing, and warehousing uses, and any use prohibited by the ELUR.

**Section 11.2 Prohibited Uses; ELUR.** No use shall be made of the Premises that (a) violates the ELUR, (b) violates any applicable law, (c) constitutes a nuisance to adjoining property owners, or (d) involves the Release of Hazardous Materials other than in compliance with Environmental Laws and customary for the operation of the Project.

**Section 11.3 Compliance with Law.** Tenant shall comply with all applicable laws, ordinances, regulations, orders, and requirements of any Governmental Authority having jurisdiction over the Premises or the Project, including zoning, building, fire, coastal, floodplain, and Environmental Laws. Tenant's obligation is subject to Landlord's obligations under Article 9 with respect to pre-existing conditions.

**Section 11.4 Landlord Approvals.** Except as expressly provided in this Lease, Landlord shall have no right to approve Tenant's use, operation, subletting, or management of the Project. Where Landlord's approval is required, Landlord shall respond within ten (10) Business Days after receipt of Tenant's request, and failure to respond shall constitute approval.

**Section 11.5 Affordable Housing Covenant.**

> (a) **Requirement.** Not fewer than fifteen percent (15%) of the residential dwelling units constructed within the Project shall be designated as affordable housing units, affordable to households earning at or below eighty percent (80%) of AMI as published annually by HUD for the applicable Port Calloway metropolitan statistical area, for the Affordable Housing Period.

> (b) **"Affordable Housing Period"** means the period commencing on the date the first residential certificate of occupancy for the Residential Tower is issued and ending on the earlier of (i) the date that is thirty (30) years thereafter, or (ii) the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease. **The Parties acknowledge that the recorded Declaration of Restrictive Covenants dated November 15, 2019 (Volume 408, Page 230) purports to impose the affordable housing requirement for the full term of any ground lease, and Landlord agrees, as a condition to the Lease Commencement Date, to execute and record an amendment to such Declaration limiting the affordable housing obligation to the Affordable Housing Period and conforming such Declaration to this Section 11.5.**

> (c) **Calculation.** The number of affordable housing units required shall be fifteen percent (15%) of the total number of residential dwelling units constructed in the Project, rounded to the nearest whole unit (with one-half unit rounded up), calculated on the basis of the residential dwelling units as of the date the first residential certificate of occupancy is issued. If the total number of residential dwelling units is subsequently changed by renovation, conversion, partial demolition, or other alteration, the required number of affordable units shall be recalculated proportionately, and Tenant shall have twelve (12) months to conform.

> (d) **Distribution and Placement.** Affordable housing units shall be (i) located on floors above the ground floor, consistent with the ELUR and Section 9.3(e), and (ii) distributed throughout the Residential Tower rather than concentrated in a single floor or area, on a unit-type basis reasonably proportionate to the market-rate unit mix (that is, the same proportion of studio, one-bedroom, two-bedroom, and three-bedroom units as exists in the market-rate mix), subject to practical constraints.

> (e) **Income Verification and Monitoring.** Tenant shall establish and administer income verification and qualification procedures reasonably consistent with applicable HUD and Connecticut Housing Finance Authority practice, and shall provide an annual compliance report to Landlord. The Parties shall designate the City's Office of Community Development (or such other entity as the Parties may agree) as the monitoring entity, with authority to inspect records (subject to applicable privacy law) and to enforce the covenant through specific performance. **Neither Landlord nor the City shall have any right of re-entry, forfeiture, or termination of this Lease by reason of a failure to comply with the affordable housing covenant, and the sole remedies for non-compliance shall be specific performance and, if Tenant fails to perform after notice and a ninety (90) day cure period, monetary damages measured by the value of the non-compliance.**

> (f) **Regulatory Agreement.** The Parties shall execute an Affordable Housing Regulatory Agreement substantially in the form attached as Exhibit K concurrently with the execution of this Lease, which shall set forth the matters described in this Section 11.5, and Landlord shall record or decline to record such agreement consistently with Section 11.5(e).

> (g) **Tax Credits.** Tenant may utilize low-income housing tax credits or other governmental incentives in connection with the affordable housing units, and Landlord shall reasonably cooperate with any application therefor, subject to Tenant's obligation to satisfy the requirements of this Section 11.5.

**Section 11.6 Conversion to Condominium or Cooperative.** Tenant shall not submit the Project, or any portion of it, to a condominium form of ownership or convert the residential units to cooperative ownership without Landlord's prior written consent, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, and which shall not be required if such conversion does not (a) result in a transfer of any interest in the fee estate, (b) impair the Leasehold Mortgagee's security, or (c) conflict with the ELUR or applicable law. **Any such conversion shall be structured so that the ground leasehold interest remains vested in a single entity (or in a structure reasonably acceptable to Landlord, the Leasehold Mortgagee, and the Issuing Title Company) and this Lease remains in full force and effect in accordance with its terms.** Landlord's consent shall be deemed given if Landlord does not respond in writing within thirty (30) days after receiving a written request that includes the proposed condominium documents and confirming that the conditions in clauses (a) through (c) are satisfied.

**Section 11.7 Signage; Name.** Tenant may install signage consistent with applicable law and the approved site plan. Landlord may not require Tenant to use or display any particular name for the Project.

**Section 11.8 Management.** Tenant shall have the exclusive right to manage and operate the Project and to engage management, leasing, and service providers, including Affiliates of Tenant, and Landlord shall have no approval right over management other than as set forth in Section 5.4(c)(iii).

**Section 11.9 Public Access and Liability.** Tenant shall maintain public access to the open space required by Section 4.8 and the pedestrian easement described in Section 4.10 consistent with the approved site plan. **Landlord shall, at its sole cost, defend, indemnify, and hold Tenant harmless from and against claims by members of the public arising from the public use of the pedestrian easement area and the open space, except to the extent caused by Tenant's negligence or willful misconduct. Landlord shall cause the City to name Tenant as an additional insured on the City's general liability program covering the public promenade and shall waive subrogation against Tenant to the extent of insurance proceeds.**

# ARTICLE 12 — ALTERATIONS, FIXTURES, AND LIENS

**Section 12.1 Right to Alter.** Tenant may, at its sole cost and expense, make alterations, additions, improvements, repairs, and replacements to the Improvements, and may demolish, reconstruct, expand, renovate, or reconfigure the Improvements, without Landlord's consent, subject to (a) compliance with applicable law, the ELUR, and this Lease; (b) any required Permit; (c) the rights of the Leasehold Mortgagee; and (d) the following notice requirements: Tenant shall deliver to Landlord not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice describing any work that involves structural changes to the Improvements or that is reasonably expected to cost more than $15,000,000, and Landlord shall have no approval right with respect to such work.

**Section 12.2 Final Ten Years.** During the final ten (10) years of the Term (from and after October 1, 2114), Tenant shall not undertake alterations, renovations, or capital improvements materially exceeding the threshold described in Section 12.1 without Landlord's prior written consent, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed and shall be deemed given if Landlord does not object in writing within twenty (20) Business Days. **Landlord's consent shall not be required for (a) any work required by applicable law, including any work required to comply with the ELUR, Environmental Laws, building codes, floodplain requirements, or coastal resilience requirements; (b) any work required to repair Casualty damage or to respond to a Condemnation; (c) any work required to maintain the structural integrity or safe operation of the Improvements; (d) any work required by a subtenant under a lease approved or permitted by this Lease; or (e) any work required by the Leasehold Mortgagee or by an insurer.**

**Section 12.3 Trade Fixtures.** Tenant may remove its Trade Fixtures at any time during the Term and at the expiration or earlier termination of the Term, provided that Tenant repairs any damage to the Premises and the Improvements caused by such removal.

**Section 12.4 Liens.** Tenant shall not permit any lien to attach to the Premises or the Improvements arising from work performed for Tenant, other than liens that Tenant causes to be discharged, bonded over, or insured over within sixty (60) days after notice. **Landlord shall have no right to subject the Premises to any mechanics' or materialmen's lien arising from work performed for Landlord.**

**Section 12.5 Ownership of Improvements.** During the Term, the Improvements shall be the property of Tenant (subject to the Leasehold Mortgage) and shall be deemed part of the realty for purposes of title insurance and applicable law. **At the expiration of the Term, and not before, the Improvements shall become the property of Landlord without payment, subject to Article 20.**

# ARTICLE 13 — MAINTENANCE AND REPAIR

**Section 13.1 Tenant's Obligations.** Tenant shall, at its sole cost and expense, maintain, repair, replace, and keep in good order and condition the Premises and the Improvements, including all building systems, roofs, facades, parking structures, site work, landscaping, the Bulkhead (subject to Section 4.11(b)), the engineered barrier (subject to Section 9.6(c)), and the open space required by Section 4.8, in each case in a manner consistent with comparable Class A mixed-use properties in the region, ordinary wear and tear, Casualty, and Condemnation excepted.

**Section 13.2 Landlord's Obligations.** Landlord shall have no obligation to maintain or repair the Premises or the Improvements arising during the Term except as expressly provided in Section 4.11(b) (Bulkhead), Section 9.4(b) (pre-existing environmental conditions), Section 9.6(c) (engineered barrier), and Section 15.3 (Casualty to the extent caused by Landlord's act).

> (b) **Umbrella or Excess Liability Insurance** with limits of not less than $50,000,000 per occurrence and in the aggregate, following form over the coverages required by clauses (a), (f), and (g);

> (c) **All-Risk (Special Form) Property Insurance** on a replacement cost basis (without deduction for depreciation), including fire, windstorm, vandalism, malicious mischief, flood, and such other risks as are customarily insured for comparable Class A properties, covering all Improvements, together with ordinance or law coverage (including coverage for the increased cost of construction required by building code changes) and, during construction, builder's risk insurance on a completed value basis covering the full value of all construction work in progress, materials, and supplies, and soft cost and delay in completion coverage in amounts reasonably determined by Tenant;

> (f) **Workers' Compensation Insurance** as required by the laws of the State of Connecticut, and Employer's Liability Insurance with limits of not less than $1,000,000;

> (g) **Business Interruption and Rental Loss Insurance** covering not less than twelve (12) months of Base Rent, Percentage Rent, and operating expenses; and

> (h) **Such other coverages** as are customarily maintained by owners or operators of comparable Class A mixed-use projects in the region, including equipment breakdown, boiler and machinery, crime, and cyber coverage.

**Section 16.2 Partial Condemnation.** If a Condemnation does not render the Premises unsuitable for the Permitted Uses, this Lease shall continue in full force and effect, Tenant shall restore the remaining Improvements to the extent practicable (using available condemnation proceeds), and Base Rent and the Breakpoint shall be equitably adjusted to reflect the reduction in the area and value of the Premises and the Improvements. **In addition, any Development Milestone deadline shall be extended by the period of delay caused by the Condemnation, and any Milestone obligation shall be equitably adjusted to reflect the reduced scope of the Project.**

> (a) **Requirement.** Not fewer than fifteen percent (15%) of the residential dwelling units constructed within the Project shall be designated as affordable housing units, affordable to households earning at or below eighty percent (80%) of AMI as published annually by HUD for the applicable Port Calloway metropolitan statistical area, for the Affordable Housing Period.

> (b) **"Affordable Housing Period"** means the period commencing on the date the first residential certificate of occupancy for the Residential Tower is issued and ending on the earlier of (i) the date that is thirty (30) years thereafter, or (ii) the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease. **The Parties acknowledge that the recorded Declaration of Restrictive Covenants dated November 15, 2019 (Volume 408, Page 230) purports to impose the affordable housing requirement for the full term of any ground lease, and Landlord agrees, as a condition to the Lease Commencement Date, to execute and record an amendment to such Declaration limiting the affordable housing obligation to the Affordable Housing Period and conforming such Declaration to this Section 11.5.**

> (c) **Calculation.** The number of affordable housing units required shall be fifteen percent (15%) of the total number of residential dwelling units constructed in the Project, rounded to the nearest whole unit (with one-half unit rounded up), calculated on the basis of the residential dwelling units as of the date the first residential certificate of occupancy is issued. > (d) **Distribution and Placement.** Affordable housing units shall be (i) located on floors above the ground floor, consistent with the ELUR and Section 9.3(e), and (ii) distributed throughout the Residential Tower rather than concentrated in a single floor or area, on a unit-type basis reasonably proportionate to the market-rate unit mix (that is, the same proportion of studio, one-bedroom, two-bedroom, and three-bedroom units as exists in the market-rate mix), subject to practical constraints.

> (f) **Regulatory Agreement.** The Parties shall execute an Affordable Housing Regulatory Agreement substantially in the form attached as Exhibit K concurrently with the execution of this Lease, which shall set forth the matters described in this Section 11.5, and Landlord shall record or decline to record such agreement consistently with Section 11.5(e).

**Section 15.3 Landlord-Caused Casualty.** If a Casualty is caused by the negligence or willful misconduct of Landlord, its agents or employees, Landlord shall be responsible for the deductible and for any uninsured loss to the extent of its liability, and rent shall abate in accordance with Section 15.2.

**Section 15.4 Tenant's Termination Rights.** Tenant may terminate this Lease upon written notice to Landlord if: (a) a Casualty renders the Premises or a material portion of the Improvements unsuitable for the Permitted Uses and restoration is not economically feasible in Tenant's reasonable judgment; (b) the cost of restoration exceeds the available insurance proceeds by more than twenty percent (20%) of the total insured value of the Improvements; (c) the Casualty occurs during the final fifteen (15) years of the Term and the cost of restoration would exceed the value of the remaining leasehold estate, as reasonably determined by Tenant; or (d) the restoration cannot reasonably be completed within thirty-six (36) months after the Casualty, taking into account applicable law, available insurance, and required permits. Any termination under this Section 15.4 shall be effective not less than sixty (60) days after notice, and Tenant shall assign to Landlord, or to the Leasehold Mortgagee at its election, all right, title, and interest in the insurance proceeds and the Improvements.

**Section 15.5 Landlord's Termination Rights.** Landlord shall have no right to terminate this Lease on account of a Casualty, except that Landlord may terminate if (a) the Casualty renders the entire Improvements untenantable, (b) Tenant has elected not to restore, and (c) Tenant has failed to commence restoration within twelve (12) months after the Casualty. Any such termination shall be subject to Section 15.6 and to the rights of the Leasehold Mortgagee.

**Section 15.6 Mortgagee Rights.** Notwithstanding Sections 15.4 and 15.5, no termination by reason of a Casualty shall be effective unless and until (a) each Leasehold Mortgagee has received thirty (30) days' prior written notice of the proposed termination and (b) the Leasehold Mortgagee has been afforded the opportunity to restore the Improvements or to designate a transferee to do so on the terms set forth in Section 17.5. Insurance proceeds shall be made available for restoration and, at the election of the Leasehold Mortgagee, applied to the Indebtedness.

**Section 15.7 Waiver of Statutory Provisions.** The Parties waive the provisions of any law that would otherwise govern the effect of a Casualty on this Lease in a manner inconsistent with this Article 15, to the extent permitted by applicable law.

# ARTICLE 16 — CONDEMNATION

**Section 16.1 Total Condemnation.** If all of the Premises, or so much of the Premises or the Improvements as renders the Premises unsuitable for the Permitted Uses, is taken by Condemnation, this Lease shall terminate as of the date title vests in the condemning authority or the condemning authority takes possession, whichever occurs first.

**Section 16.2 Partial Condemnation.** If a Condemnation does not render the Premises unsuitable for the Permitted Uses, this Lease shall continue in full force and effect, Tenant shall restore the remaining Improvements to the extent practicable (using available condemnation proceeds), and Base Rent and the Breakpoint shall be equitably adjusted to reflect the reduction in the area and value of the Premises and the Improvements. **In addition, any Development Milestone deadline shall be extended by the period of delay caused by the Condemnation, and any Milestone obligation shall be equitably adjusted to reflect the reduced scope of the Project.**

**Section 16.3 Allocation of Award.** **The award in any Condemnation shall be allocated as follows: (a) Landlord shall receive the portion of the award attributable to the value of the fee interest in the land, determined as the value of the land unimproved and unencumbered by this Lease; (b) Tenant shall receive the portion of the award attributable to the value of the leasehold estate and the Improvements, determined in accordance with the appraisal procedure set forth in Section 5.6, applied mutatis mutandis; and (c) Tenant shall receive, in addition, any award or payment for Trade Fixtures, personal property, business interruption, moving expenses, loss of goodwill, and relocation expenses, which amounts shall not be shared with Landlord.**

**Section 16.4 Separate Claims.** Landlord and Tenant shall each have the right to file a separate claim for the portion of the award allocated to it under Section 16.3, and each Party shall cooperate with the other in the prosecution of such claims. **Neither Party shall settle its claim in a manner that adversely affects the other Party's claim without the other Party's written consent.**

**Section 16.5 Payment to Leasehold Mortgagee.** Any portion of the award payable to Tenant shall be paid to the Leasehold Mortgagee to the extent of the Indebtedness, or as otherwise directed under the SNDA. Landlord shall have no claim to any portion of the award allocable to the Leasehold Mortgagee's interest.

**Section 16.6 Temporary Taking.** A temporary taking of all or any portion of the Premises shall not terminate this Lease, and Tenant shall be entitled to the entire award for the period of the temporary taking, subject to Section 16.5.

**Section 16.7 Definition.** **"Condemnation"** means any taking of all or any portion of the Premises, the Improvements, or Tenant's leasehold estate, by eminent domain or condemnation, or any conveyance in lieu thereof under threat of condemnation, by any Governmental Authority having the power of eminent domain.
