# ARTICLE 17 — LEASEHOLD FINANCING AND LEASEHOLD MORTGAGEE PROTECTIONS

**Section 17.1 Right to Encumber.** **Tenant may grant one or more Leasehold Mortgages encumbering Tenant's entire leasehold estate in the Premises and the Improvements to any Leasehold Mortgagee, without the prior consent, approval, or joinder of Landlord and without the payment of any consent fee, administrative charge, or other compensation to Landlord.** No approval, consent, or other condition from Landlord shall be required for the granting, recording, enforcement, foreclosure, or assignment of any Leasehold Mortgage. A Leasehold Mortgage may encumber the entire leasehold estate created by this Lease, together with all Improvements, fixtures, and appurtenances now or hereafter constructed on the Premises, and all subleases, rents, and revenues, and Tenant may execute a collateral assignment of leases and rents and an assignment of construction contracts and plans in favor of the Leasehold Mortgagee, all without Landlord's consent.

**Section 17.2 Notice to Landlord.** Tenant shall give Landlord written notice of the granting of any Leasehold Mortgage within fifteen (15) Business Days after its execution, identifying the Leasehold Mortgagee, the original principal amount, and the notice address for such Leasehold Mortgagee. **Landlord shall, upon request, execute a reasonable acknowledgment of a Leasehold Mortgage and a consent to collateral assignment, at no cost to Tenant or the Leasehold Mortgagee.**

**Section 17.3 Recognition of Leasehold Mortgagee.** Upon receipt of the notice contemplated by Section 17.2, Landlord shall recognize the named Leasehold Mortgagee as entitled to the rights set forth in this Article 17. Landlord shall maintain a current list of Leasehold Mortgagees and shall deliver to each Leasehold Mortgagee, at the address designated in its notice, copies of all notices, demands, and other communications delivered to Tenant under this Lease, **simultaneously** with delivery to Tenant. **Any notice of default or notice of termination delivered to Tenant without simultaneous delivery to each Leasehold Mortgagee shall be void and of no effect.** Each Leasehold Mortgagee shall designate its notice address and may change it by written notice to Landlord and Tenant. Bayside Federal Lending Corp.'s initial notice address is: 200 Atlantic Boulevard, Stamford, Connecticut 06902, Attention: Sandra Milliken, Senior Vice President, Commercial Real Estate Lending, with a copy to Lender's counsel at the address Lender designates.

**Section 17.4 SNDA.** **Landlord shall execute and deliver to Tenant and each Leasehold Mortgagee, simultaneously with or prior to the first advance of the construction loan and in any event on or before the Lease Commencement Date, a Subordination, Non-Disturbance, and Attornment Agreement substantially in the form attached as Exhibit E and in form and substance reasonably acceptable to the Leasehold Mortgagee, which shall contain at a minimum:**

> (a) Landlord's acknowledgment of the existence and first priority of the Leasehold Mortgage and recognition of the Leasehold Mortgagee's interest in Tenant's leasehold estate and the Improvements;

> (b) Landlord's agreement not to disturb the Leasehold Mortgagee's security interest, or the rights of any purchaser at a foreclosure sale or transferee pursuant to a deed in lieu of foreclosure, in this Lease or the Improvements, so long as the obligations of Tenant under this Lease are performed (or cured by the Leasehold Mortgagee);

> (c) Landlord's agreement to recognize the Leasehold Mortgagee, its designee, or any purchaser at foreclosure or transferee under a deed in lieu of foreclosure, as Tenant under this Lease upon the same terms and conditions as this Lease, without Landlord's approval and without any transfer fee;

> (d) the Leasehold Mortgagee's cure rights and notice rights set forth in Sections 5.4 and 17.6;

> (e) the New Lease right set forth in Section 17.5;

> (f) the prohibition on voluntary surrender and amendment set forth in Section 17.7;

> (g) the Leasehold Mortgagee's rights with respect to Casualty and Condemnation proceeds and restoration; and

> (h) such additional provisions as the Leasehold Mortgagee may reasonably require.

**Landlord shall execute and deliver an SNDA (or a replacement or amendment) in favor of any successor or additional Leasehold Mortgagee, including any refinancing lender, upon request and without fee, on the same terms as Exhibit E, within fifteen (15) Business Days after request.** Landlord shall also execute such estoppel certificates as are reasonably requested in connection with any financing, refinancing, or sale, in the form attached as Exhibit G, within ten (10) Business Days after request, certifying as to the matters reasonably requested and as to which Landlord can certify consistent with the facts.

**Section 17.5 New Lease Right.** **If this Lease is terminated for any reason whatsoever — including without limitation a Tenant Event of Default, a Reverter Termination, surrender, rejection in bankruptcy, or operation of law — the Leasehold Mortgagee (or its designee) shall have the right, upon written request delivered to Landlord within sixty (60) days after the Leasehold Mortgagee's receipt of notice of such termination, to enter into a new ground lease of the Premises (the "New Lease") with Landlord on the same terms and conditions as this Lease (including the same Base Rent, the same Term as the remainder of the original Term, and the same rights and obligations), provided that:**

> (a) the Leasehold Mortgagee (or its designee) cures all monetary defaults then existing under this Lease within sixty (60) days after the effective date of the New Lease;

> (b) the Leasehold Mortgagee (or its designee) cures all non-monetary defaults that are reasonably susceptible of cure within ninety (90) days after the effective date of the New Lease, or, if such cure cannot reasonably be completed within such period, commences such cure within such ninety (90) day period and thereafter diligently and continuously pursues cure to completion within a reasonable time, but in no event more than one hundred eighty (180) days after the effective date of the New Lease;

> (c) the Leasehold Mortgagee (or its designee) assumes all obligations under the New Lease prospectively from the effective date of the New Lease; and

> (d) the New Lease provides that all subleases, licenses, and occupancy agreements entered into by Tenant or any subtenant before the termination of this Lease shall be recognized by Landlord.

**Landlord shall execute and deliver the New Lease within thirty (30) days after the Leasehold Mortgagee's written request, and the New Lease shall be effective as of the date of termination of this Lease and shall have a priority in all respects equal to the priority of this Lease.** The New Lease shall not require the payment of any transfer fee, consent fee, or premium to Landlord, and the Leasehold Mortgagee shall not be required to pay any Rent for any period prior to the termination of this Lease except to the extent of any monetary default cured under clause (a). **Landlord's obligation to enter into a New Lease shall not be conditioned on the Leasehold Mortgagee's payment of any amount in excess of the amounts described in clauses (a) through (c).** The form of the New Lease and the related Leasehold Mortgagee recognition provisions are attached as Exhibit F.

**Section 17.6 Leasehold Mortgagee Cure Rights.** No termination of this Lease (whether under Article 5, Article 19, or otherwise) shall be effective unless and until each Leasehold Mortgagee has received the notice required by Section 17.3 and the applicable cure periods set forth below have expired without cure by the Leasehold Mortgagee:

> (a) **Monetary Defaults.** The Leasehold Mortgagee shall have sixty (60) days from its receipt of notice of any monetary default to cure such default on behalf of Tenant. **The Leasehold Mortgagee may cure any monetary default without regard to whether the Leasehold Mortgagee has commenced foreclosure, and Landlord shall accept cure by a Leasehold Mortgagee as if performed by Tenant.**

> (b) **Non-Monetary Defaults.** The Leasehold Mortgagee shall have ninety (90) days from its receipt of notice of any non-monetary default to cure such default, or, if such cure cannot reasonably be completed within such ninety (90) day period, the Leasehold Mortgagee shall have commenced cure within such period and shall thereafter diligently and continuously pursue cure to completion within a reasonable time not to exceed one hundred eighty (180) days after its receipt of notice.

> (c) **Milestone Defaults.** The Leasehold Mortgagee's cure period with respect to a Milestone failure shall be the Mortgagee Cure Period described in Section 5.4(b), and the Leasehold Mortgagee may cure in the manner described in Section 5.4(c).

> (d) **Post-Foreclosure Cure.** If the Leasehold Mortgagee or its designee acquires Tenant's leasehold estate through foreclosure, deed in lieu of foreclosure, or assignment, the Leasehold Mortgagee shall have an additional sixty (60) days after such acquisition to cure any defaults that were not cured before such acquisition, and no termination shall be effective during such period.

> (e) **Additional Period; Run.** **The cure periods set forth in this Section 17.6 shall run in addition to, and not concurrently with, any cure periods afforded to Tenant under this Lease.** Landlord shall accept cure by the Leasehold Mortgagee as if such cure had been performed by Tenant.

> (f) **No Termination for Matters the Mortgagee Cannot Cure.** Landlord shall not terminate this Lease on account of any default that is not reasonably susceptible of cure by the Leasehold Mortgagee (including any default consisting of Tenant's bankruptcy filing or insolvency) unless and until the Leasehold Mortgagee has been afforded the rights set forth in Section 17.9 and Section 17.5.

**Section 17.7 No Voluntary Surrender; No Amendment Without Mortgagee Consent.** **For so long as any Leasehold Mortgage remains in effect, Landlord shall not accept a voluntary surrender, cancellation, or termination of this Lease from Tenant, and Landlord and Tenant shall not amend, modify, supplement, or terminate this Lease in any material respect, without the prior written consent of each Leasehold Mortgagee. Any purported surrender, amendment, modification, supplement, or termination effected without such consent shall be void and of no force or effect as against the Leasehold Mortgagee, and this Lease shall continue in full force and effect as if such purported action had not occurred.** "Material" amendments include any amendment to Rent, the Term, the Permitted Uses, the reverter and Improvement Compensation provisions, the New Lease right, the cure periods, or the Security Deposit. Non-material amendments (including administrative corrections and changes to notice addresses) shall not require Leasehold Mortgagee consent.

**Section 17.8 Foreclosure and Assignment.** **The Leasehold Mortgagee shall have the unconditional right to foreclose the Leasehold Mortgage (whether by judicial foreclosure, power of sale, or otherwise), to accept a deed in lieu of foreclosure, and to assign this Lease and the leasehold estate to a qualified transferee at or following any foreclosure sale or deed-in-lieu transfer, in each case without the prior consent of Landlord.** Any such transferee shall meet the objective financial and experience qualifications set forth in Section 18.4. **Landlord shall recognize any such transferee as Tenant under this Lease and shall not unreasonably withhold, condition, or delay such recognition, and shall execute any documents reasonably requested by the Leasehold Mortgagee to effectuate or confirm the foreclosure, transfer, or assignment, including a written assumption of this Lease by the transferee.** No foreclosure, deed-in-lieu transfer, assignment by or to a Leasehold Mortgagee, or transfer to a designee or affiliate of a Leasehold Mortgagee shall constitute a Transfer requiring Landlord's consent or trigger the Right of First Refusal described in Article 18.

**Section 17.9 Bankruptcy Protections.**

> (a) If Tenant becomes a debtor in any proceeding under Title 11 of the United States Code or any similar state insolvency law, the Leasehold Mortgagee shall have the right (i) to request that any trustee, debtor in possession, or other party in interest assume or reject this Lease in a timely manner consistent with 11 U.S.C. § 365; (ii) to cure any defaults under this Lease and to provide adequate assurance of future performance on behalf of Tenant to the extent necessary to prevent rejection of this Lease; and (iii) to seek an extension of time within which to assume this Lease under 11 U.S.C. § 365(d)(4) and any applicable order.

> (b) **The New Lease right set forth in Section 17.5 shall survive rejection of this Lease in bankruptcy to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, and Landlord shall recognize the Leasehold Mortgagee's right to obtain a New Lease notwithstanding such rejection.**

> (c) **Tenant's rights under 11 U.S.C. § 365(h) to retain its leasehold estate, and the Leasehold Mortgagee's rights under this Article 17, shall not be impaired by any provision of this Lease. Landlord expressly acknowledges Tenant's rights under 11 U.S.C. § 365(h)(1)(A)(ii) and agrees that Tenant's possessory rights and its right to enforce Landlord's obligations may be retained notwithstanding rejection.**

> (d) **Any provision of this Lease that would terminate, modify, or permit the modification of this Lease solely by reason of Tenant's insolvency or the commencement of a bankruptcy proceeding (an "ipso facto" provision) shall be enforceable only to the extent enforceable under 11 U.S.C. § 365(e) and applicable law.**

**Section 17.10 Multiple Leasehold Mortgagees; Successor Mortgagee.** If more than one Leasehold Mortgage is outstanding, the Leasehold Mortgagee holding the most senior Leasehold Mortgage shall be entitled to exercise the rights under this Article 17, and each other Leasehold Mortgagee shall be entitled to the notice and cure rights in a manner consistent with the intercreditor priorities. A Leasehold Mortgagee that assigns its Leasehold Mortgage shall be discharged from its obligations under this Article 17, and its assignee shall succeed to its rights. Landlord shall recognize any such assignee upon notice.

**Section 17.11 Subordination of Landlord's Fee Encumbrances; Non-Disturbance.** In addition to Section 3.9, Landlord shall, upon Tenant's or any Leasehold Mortgagee's request, cause any holder of a mortgage or deed of trust encumbering Landlord's fee interest, and any other Person holding an interest senior to this Lease, to execute a subordination and non-disturbance agreement recognizing this Lease and the Leasehold Mortgage and agreeing not to disturb them. **This Lease shall be senior to any such encumbrance, and any fee mortgagee that forecloses shall take the fee interest subject to this Lease.**

**Section 17.12 Proceeds.** Insurance proceeds payable on account of damage to the Improvements shall be made available for restoration and, at the election of the Leasehold Mortgagee, applied to the Indebtedness. Condemnation proceeds allocable to Tenant under Section 16.3 shall be paid to the Leasehold Mortgagee to the extent of the Indebtedness or as the SNDA provides. Landlord shall have no claim to any such proceeds except as provided in Section 16.3(a).

**Section 17.13 Cooperation; Fees.** Landlord shall cooperate with Tenant and each Leasehold Mortgagee in connection with any financing, refinancing, foreclosure, or sale of the leasehold estate, and shall execute such consents, estoppels, SNDAs, recognition agreements, and assumptions as are reasonably requested, in each case without the payment of any fee, cost, or charge other than reimbursement of Landlord's reasonable out-of-pocket attorneys' fees not exceeding $7,500 per instrument. **Landlord shall have no right to review, approve, or comment on the terms of any Leasehold Mortgage, loan document, or financing arrangement between Tenant and a Leasehold Mortgagee.**

# ARTICLE 18 — TRANSFERS, SUBLETTING, AND RIGHT OF FIRST REFUSAL

**Section 18.1 Definition of Transfer.** **"Transfer"** means any assignment, conveyance, or other transfer of this Lease or of any leasehold estate or interest in the Premises, whether voluntarily, involuntarily, or by operation of law, and any change in control of Tenant. A Transfer does not include (a) a sublease of space in the ordinary course of the operation of the Project; (b) the grant of any Leasehold Mortgage; (c) any transfer to a Leasehold Mortgagee, its designee, or a purchaser at foreclosure or under a deed in lieu of foreclosure; or (d) any transfer described in Section 18.3.

**Section 18.2 Consent Required for Transfers.** Tenant shall not effect a Transfer to a Person that is not an Affiliate without Landlord's prior written consent, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed and shall be subject to Landlord's Right of First Refusal in Section 18.5. **Landlord shall respond to a written request for consent within thirty (30) days after receipt of the request and all reasonably requested information; if Landlord fails to respond within such period, consent shall be deemed given.** Any purported Transfer in violation of this Article 18 shall be void.

**Section 18.3 Permitted Transfers.** **No consent of Landlord and no Right of First Refusal shall apply to any of the following (each a "Permitted Transfer"):**

> (a) any Transfer to an Affiliate of Tenant;

> (b) any Transfer to Coventry Capital Partners LP, its affiliates, related funds, or any entity managed or advised by Coventry Capital Partners LP or its affiliates, or to Marcus Ellison or his estate planning vehicles;

> (c) any grant of a Leasehold Mortgage, and any Transfer to or by a Leasehold Mortgagee or its designee, including any foreclosure, deed in lieu of foreclosure, assignment, or transfer in connection with the exercise of remedies;

> (d) any Transfer resulting from a merger, consolidation, or reorganization of Tenant, provided the surviving entity assumes this Lease;

> (e) any public offering, private placement, or transfer of direct or indirect equity interests in Tenant or any of its direct or indirect owners, including any transfer of limited partner interests, membership interests, or interests in a real estate investment trust, fund, or similar vehicle;

> (f) any Transfer to a Person that acquires all or substantially all of Tenant's assets or equity, provided such Person (i) has a tangible net worth of not less than the greater of (A) $75,000,000 and (B) the amount of Tenant's net worth at the time of the Transfer, and (ii) has, together with its affiliates, not less than ten (10) years' experience developing, owning, or operating mixed-use properties of comparable size in the Northeast;

> (g) any Transfer pursuant to a plan of reorganization, dissolution, or liquidation effected in compliance with Article 18; and

> (h) any Transfer to a governmental entity or authority.

**Section 18.4 Objective Qualification Standards.** For purposes of Section 17.8 and Section 18.3(f), a **"qualified transferee"** is a Person that (a) has a tangible net worth, determined in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, of not less than $75,000,000 (or, if the transferee is an institutional investor, managed funds or committed capital of not less than $250,000,000), (b) together with its affiliates has not less than ten (10) years' experience developing, owning, or operating mixed-use or multifamily properties of comparable size and quality, and (c) is not a Person with whom Landlord is prohibited from transacting business under applicable law.

**Section 18.5 Right of First Refusal.**

> (a) **Grant.** During the first twenty (20) years of the Term (that is, from the Lease Commencement Date through September 30, 2045), if Tenant proposes to Transfer this Lease to a Person that is not an Affiliate (and the proposed Transfer is not a Permitted Transfer), Landlord shall have a right of first refusal (the **"Right of First Refusal"**) to acquire the leasehold interest on the same terms and conditions as the proposed Transfer.

> (b) **Notice.** Tenant shall deliver to Landlord a written notice (an **"Assignment Notice"**) setting forth the identity of the proposed transferee, the material terms of the proposed Transfer (including price), and a copy of the proposed assignment agreement or letter of intent (redacted to remove confidential or competitively sensitive information).

> (c) **Exercise.** Landlord shall have sixty (60) days after receipt of the Assignment Notice to exercise the Right of First Refusal by written notice to Tenant. **If Landlord does not exercise within such period, or if Landlord exercises but fails to close within ninety (90) days thereafter (subject only to customary closing conditions), the Right of First Refusal shall lapse with respect to such proposed Transfer, and Tenant may proceed with the Transfer to the identified transferee on terms no more favorable to the transferee than those set forth in the Assignment Notice. If the Transfer does not close within one hundred eighty (180) days after the Assignment Notice, the Right of First Refusal shall be reinstated.**

> (d) **Exclusions.** **The Right of First Refusal shall not apply to, and shall be deemed waived with respect to, any Permitted Transfer, including without limitation any grant of a Leasehold Mortgage, any foreclosure, deed in lieu of foreclosure, or other exercise of remedies by a Leasehold Mortgagee, any assignment by a Leasehold Mortgagee or its designee, and any Transfer to an Affiliate.**

> (e) **No Restraint on Financing.** **Landlord acknowledges and agrees that the Right of First Refusal shall not apply to, delay, condition, or otherwise impair (i) the granting, recording, administration, enforcement, or foreclosure of any Leasehold Mortgage, (ii) any collateral assignment of leases and rents, (iii) any pledge of Tenant's direct or indirect ownership interests in favor of a Leasehold Mortgagee, or (iv) any Transfer effected in connection with any of the foregoing.** Any provision of this Lease or of any recorded instrument to the contrary shall not apply to the matters described in this Section 18.5(e), and Landlord shall be deemed to have waived the Right of First Refusal with respect to such matters.

**Section 18.6 Amendment of Recorded Right of First Refusal.** **The Parties acknowledge that the Declaration of Right of First Refusal dated September 8, 2019 and recorded at Volume 405, Page 55 of the Port Calloway Land Records (the "Recorded ROFR") does not, by its terms, contain any exception or carve-out for transfers resulting from foreclosure, deed in lieu of foreclosure, the exercise of remedies by a leasehold mortgagee, or assignments by a leasehold mortgagee or its designee following a foreclosure or acceptance of a deed in lieu. As a condition to the Lease Commencement Date, Landlord shall execute, acknowledge, and record an amendment to the Recorded ROFR (in form reasonably satisfactory to Tenant and each Leasehold Mortgagee) that (a) incorporates the exceptions set forth in Sections 18.3 and 18.5, (b) confirms that the Recorded ROFR applies only to a Transfer of this Lease and not to any Leasehold Mortgage, collateral assignment, or pledge, and (c) confirms that the Recorded ROFR will not be asserted against any Leasehold Mortgagee, any purchaser at foreclosure, any transferee under a deed in lieu of foreclosure, or any designee or affiliate of any of them. Landlord shall deliver such recorded amendment, together with evidence of recordation, on or before the Lease Commencement Date.**

**Section 18.7 Subletting.** Tenant may sublease or license space within the Project to residential, office, and retail tenants in the ordinary course of business without Landlord's consent. **A sublease of all or substantially all of the Premises to a single subtenant shall require Landlord's consent only if such sublease is for a term exceeding twenty-five (25) years, and in such case Landlord's consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed and Landlord may not exercise the Right of First Refusal in respect thereof. Landlord shall have no right to approve the identity, creditworthiness, or rent of any subtenant, or to review any sublease.**

**Section 18.8 No Release.** No Transfer shall release Tenant from its obligations under this Lease accruing prior to the Transfer, except that a Transfer of this Lease in compliance with this Article 18 shall release the transferor from obligations accruing after the date of the Transfer, provided the transferee assumes this Lease in writing.

**Section 18.9 Landlord's Transfer of Fee Interest.** Landlord may not transfer its fee interest in the Premises except subject to this Lease, and any transferee shall be deemed to have assumed Landlord's obligations under this Lease. Landlord shall deliver written notice to Tenant and each Leasehold Mortgagee within ten (10) Business Days after any transfer of its fee interest. **Landlord shall not be released from liability for obligations arising prior to the transfer.**

**Section 18.10 Right of First Opportunity to Purchase Fee.** **If at any time during the Term Landlord proposes to sell, convey, or otherwise dispose of its fee interest in the Premises to a Person other than a Governmental Authority, Tenant shall have a right of first opportunity to purchase the fee interest on the same terms as the proposed disposition, exercisable by written notice within thirty (30) days after receipt of Landlord's notice describing the proposed terms.** This Section 18.10 shall not apply to (a) any transfer to a Governmental Authority, (b) any transfer required by law, or (c) any encumbrance or mortgage.

**Section 17.4 SNDA.** **Landlord shall execute and deliver to Tenant and each Leasehold Mortgagee, simultaneously with or prior to the first advance of the construction loan and in any event on or before the Lease Commencement Date, a Subordination, Non-Disturbance, and Attornment Agreement substantially in the form attached as Exhibit E and in form and substance reasonably acceptable to the Leasehold Mortgagee, which shall contain at a minimum:**

> (a) Landlord's acknowledgment of the existence and first priority of the Leasehold Mortgage and recognition of the Leasehold Mortgagee's interest in Tenant's leasehold estate and the Improvements;

> (b) Landlord's agreement not to disturb the Leasehold Mortgagee's security interest, or the rights of any purchaser at a foreclosure sale or transferee pursuant to a deed in lieu of foreclosure, in this Lease or the Improvements, so long as the obligations of Tenant under this Lease are performed (or cured by the Leasehold Mortgagee);

> (c) Landlord's agreement to recognize the Leasehold Mortgagee, its designee, or any purchaser at foreclosure or transferee under a deed in lieu of foreclosure, as Tenant under this Lease upon the same terms and conditions as this Lease, without Landlord's approval and without any transfer fee;

> (d) the Leasehold Mortgagee's cure rights and notice rights set forth in Sections 5.4 and 17.6;

> (e) the New Lease right set forth in Section 17.5;

> (f) the prohibition on voluntary surrender and amendment set forth in Section 17.7;

> (g) the Leasehold Mortgagee's rights with respect to Casualty and Condemnation proceeds and restoration; and

> (h) such additional provisions as the Leasehold Mortgagee may reasonably require.

**Landlord shall execute and deliver an SNDA (or a replacement or amendment) in favor of any successor or additional Leasehold Mortgagee, including any refinancing lender, upon request and without fee, on the same terms as Exhibit E, within fifteen (15) Business Days after request.** Landlord shall also execute such estoppel certificates as are reasonably requested in connection with any financing, refinancing, or sale, in the form attached as Exhibit G, within ten (10) Business Days after request, certifying as to the matters reasonably requested and as to which Landlord can certify consistent with the facts.

**Section 17.5 New Lease Right.** **If this Lease is terminated for any reason whatsoever — including without limitation a Tenant Event of Default, a Reverter Termination, surrender, rejection in bankruptcy, or operation of law — the Leasehold Mortgagee (or its designee) shall have the right, upon written request delivered to Landlord within sixty (60) days after the Leasehold Mortgagee's receipt of notice of such termination, to enter into a new ground lease of the Premises (the "New Lease") with Landlord on the same terms and conditions as this Lease (including the same Base Rent, the same Term as the remainder of the original Term, and the same rights and obligations), provided that:**

> (a) the Leasehold Mortgagee (or its designee) cures all monetary defaults then existing under this Lease within sixty (60) days after the effective date of the New Lease;

> (b) the Leasehold Mortgagee (or its designee) cures all non-monetary defaults that are reasonably susceptible of cure within ninety (90) days after the effective date of the New Lease, or, if such cure cannot reasonably be completed within such period, commences such cure within such ninety (90) day period and thereafter diligently and continuously pursues cure to completion within a reasonable time, but in no event more than one hundred eighty (180) days after the effective date of the New Lease;

> (c) the Leasehold Mortgagee (or its designee) assumes all obligations under the New Lease prospectively from the effective date of the New Lease; and

> (d) the New Lease provides that all subleases, licenses, and occupancy agreements entered into by Tenant or any subtenant before the termination of this Lease shall be recognized by Landlord.

**Landlord shall execute and deliver the New Lease within thirty (30) days after the Leasehold Mortgagee's written request, and the New Lease shall be effective as of the date of termination of this Lease and shall have a priority in all respects equal to the priority of this Lease.** The New Lease shall not require the payment of any transfer fee, consent fee, or premium to Landlord, and the Leasehold Mortgagee shall not be required to pay any Rent for any period prior to the termination of this Lease except to the extent of any monetary default cured under clause (a). **Landlord's obligation to enter into a New Lease shall not be conditioned on the Leasehold Mortgagee's payment of any amount in excess of the amounts described in clauses (a) through (c).** The form of the New Lease and the related Leasehold Mortgagee recognition provisions are attached as Exhibit F.

**Section 17.6 Leasehold Mortgagee Cure Rights.** No termination of this Lease (whether under Article 5, Article 19, or otherwise) shall be effective unless and until each Leasehold Mortgagee has received the notice required by Section 17.3 and the applicable cure periods set forth below have expired without cure by the Leasehold Mortgagee:

> (a) **Monetary Defaults.** The Leasehold Mortgagee shall have sixty (60) days from its receipt of notice of any monetary default to cure such default on behalf of Tenant. **The Leasehold Mortgagee may cure any monetary default without regard to whether the Leasehold Mortgagee has commenced foreclosure, and Landlord shall accept cure by a Leasehold Mortgagee as if performed by Tenant.**

> (b) **Non-Monetary Defaults.** The Leasehold Mortgagee shall have ninety (90) days from its receipt of notice of any non-monetary default to cure such default, or, if such cure cannot reasonably be completed within such ninety (90) day period, the Leasehold Mortgagee shall have commenced cure within such period and shall thereafter diligently and continuously pursue cure to completion within a reasonable time not to exceed one hundred eighty (180) days after its receipt of notice.

> (c) **Milestone Defaults.** The Leasehold Mortgagee's cure period with respect to a Milestone failure shall be the Mortgagee Cure Period described in Section 5.4(b), and the Leasehold Mortgagee may cure in the manner described in Section 5.4(c).

> (d) **Post-Foreclosure Cure.** If the Leasehold Mortgagee or its designee acquires Tenant's leasehold estate through foreclosure, deed in lieu of foreclosure, or assignment, the Leasehold Mortgagee shall have an additional sixty (60) days after such acquisition to cure any defaults that were not cured before such acquisition, and no termination shall be effective during such period.

> (e) **Additional Period; Run.** **The cure periods set forth in this Section 17.6 shall run in addition to, and not concurrently with, any cure periods afforded to Tenant under this Lease.** Landlord shall accept cure by the Leasehold Mortgagee as if such cure had been performed by Tenant.

> (f) **No Termination for Matters the Mortgagee Cannot Cure.** Landlord shall not terminate this Lease on account of any default that is not reasonably susceptible of cure by the Leasehold Mortgagee (including any default consisting of Tenant's bankruptcy filing or insolvency) unless and until the Leasehold Mortgagee has been afforded the rights set forth in Section 17.9 and Section 17.5.

**Section 17.7 No Voluntary Surrender; No Amendment Without Mortgagee Consent.** **For so long as any Leasehold Mortgage remains in effect, Landlord shall not accept a voluntary surrender, cancellation, or termination of this Lease from Tenant, and Landlord and Tenant shall not amend, modify, supplement, or terminate this Lease in any material respect, without the prior written consent of each Leasehold Mortgagee. Any purported surrender, amendment, modification, supplement, or termination effected without such consent shall be void and of no force or effect as against the Leasehold Mortgagee, and this Lease shall continue in full force and effect as if such purported action had not occurred.** "Material" amendments include any amendment to Rent, the Term, the Permitted Uses, the reverter and Improvement Compensation provisions, the New Lease right, the cure periods, or the Security Deposit. Non-material amendments (including administrative corrections and changes to notice addresses) shall not require Leasehold Mortgagee consent.

**Section 17.8 Foreclosure and Assignment.** **The Leasehold Mortgagee shall have the unconditional right to foreclose the Leasehold Mortgage (whether by judicial foreclosure, power of sale, or otherwise), to accept a deed in lieu of foreclosure, and to assign this Lease and the leasehold estate to a qualified transferee at or following any foreclosure sale or deed-in-lieu transfer, in each case without the prior consent of Landlord.** Any such transferee shall meet the objective financial and experience qualifications set forth in Section 18.4. **Landlord shall recognize any such transferee as Tenant under this Lease and shall not unreasonably withhold, condition, or delay such recognition, and shall execute any documents reasonably requested by the Leasehold Mortgagee to effectuate or confirm the foreclosure, transfer, or assignment, including a written assumption of this Lease by the transferee.** No foreclosure, deed-in-lieu transfer, assignment by or to a Leasehold Mortgagee, or transfer to a designee or affiliate of a Leasehold Mortgagee shall constitute a Transfer requiring Landlord's consent or trigger the Right of First Refusal described in Article 18.

**Section 17.9 Bankruptcy Protections.**

> (a) If Tenant becomes a debtor in any proceeding under Title 11 of the United States Code or any similar state insolvency law, the Leasehold Mortgagee shall have the right (i) to request that any trustee, debtor in possession, or other party in interest assume or reject this Lease in a timely manner consistent with 11 U.S.C. § 365; (ii) to cure any defaults under this Lease and to provide adequate assurance of future performance on behalf of Tenant to the extent necessary to prevent rejection of this Lease; and (iii) to seek an extension of time within which to assume this Lease under 11 U.S.C. § 365(d)(4) and any applicable order.

> (b) **The New Lease right set forth in Section 17.5 shall survive rejection of this Lease in bankruptcy to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, and Landlord shall recognize the Leasehold Mortgagee's right to obtain a New Lease notwithstanding such rejection.**

> (c) **Tenant's rights under 11 U.S.C. § 365(h) to retain its leasehold estate, and the Leasehold Mortgagee's rights under this Article 17, shall not be impaired by any provision of this Lease. Landlord expressly acknowledges Tenant's rights under 11 U.S.C. § 365(h)(1)(A)(ii) and agrees that Tenant's possessory rights and its right to enforce Landlord's obligations may be retained notwithstanding rejection.**

> (d) **Any provision of this Lease that would terminate, modify, or permit the modification of this Lease solely by reason of Tenant's insolvency or the commencement of a bankruptcy proceeding (an "ipso facto" provision) shall be enforceable only to the extent enforceable under 11 U.S.C. § 365(e) and applicable law.**

**Section 17.10 Multiple Leasehold Mortgagees; Successor Mortgagee.** If more than one Leasehold Mortgage is outstanding, the Leasehold Mortgagee holding the most senior Leasehold Mortgage shall be entitled to exercise the rights under this Article 17, and each other Leasehold Mortgagee shall be entitled to the notice and cure rights in a manner consistent with the intercreditor priorities. A Leasehold Mortgagee that assigns its Leasehold Mortgage shall be discharged from its obligations under this Article 17, and its assignee shall succeed to its rights. Landlord shall recognize any such assignee upon notice.

**Section 17.11 Subordination of Landlord's Fee Encumbrances; Non-Disturbance.** In addition to Section 3.9, Landlord shall, upon Tenant's or any Leasehold Mortgagee's request, cause any holder of a mortgage or deed of trust encumbering Landlord's fee interest, and any other Person holding an interest senior to this Lease, to execute a subordination and non-disturbance agreement recognizing this Lease and the Leasehold Mortgage and agreeing not to disturb them. **This Lease shall be senior to any such encumbrance, and any fee mortgagee that forecloses shall take the fee interest subject to this Lease.**

**Section 17.12 Proceeds.** Insurance proceeds payable on account of damage to the Improvements shall be made available for restoration and, at the election of the Leasehold Mortgagee, applied to the Indebtedness. Condemnation proceeds allocable to Tenant under Section 16.3 shall be paid to the Leasehold Mortgagee to the extent of the Indebtedness or as the SNDA provides. Landlord shall have no claim to any such proceeds except as provided in Section 16.3(a).

**Section 17.13 Cooperation; Fees.** Landlord shall cooperate with Tenant and each Leasehold Mortgagee in connection with any financing, refinancing, foreclosure, or sale of the leasehold estate, and shall execute such consents, estoppels, SNDAs, recognition agreements, and assumptions as are reasonably requested, in each case without the payment of any fee, cost, or charge other than reimbursement of Landlord's reasonable out-of-pocket attorneys' fees not exceeding $7,500 per instrument. **Landlord shall have no right to review, approve, or comment on the terms of any Leasehold Mortgage, loan document, or financing arrangement between Tenant and a Leasehold Mortgagee.**

# ARTICLE 18 — TRANSFERS, SUBLETTING, AND RIGHT OF FIRST REFUSAL

**Section 18.1 Definition of Transfer.** **"Transfer"** means any assignment, conveyance, or other transfer of this Lease or of any leasehold estate or interest in the Premises, whether voluntarily, involuntarily, or by operation of law, and any change in control of Tenant. A Transfer does not include (a) a sublease of space in the ordinary course of the operation of the Project; (b) the grant of any Leasehold Mortgage; (c) any transfer to a Leasehold Mortgagee, its designee, or a purchaser at foreclosure or under a deed in lieu of foreclosure; or (d) any transfer described in Section 18.3.

**Section 18.2 Consent Required for Transfers.** Tenant shall not effect a Transfer to a Person that is not an Affiliate without Landlord's prior written consent, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed and shall be subject to Landlord's Right of First Refusal in Section 18.5. **Landlord shall respond to a written request for consent within thirty (30) days after receipt of the request and all reasonably requested information; if Landlord fails to respond within such period, consent shall be deemed given.** Any purported Transfer in violation of this Article 18 shall be void.

**Section 18.3 Permitted Transfers.** **No consent of Landlord and no Right of First Refusal shall apply to any of the following (each a "Permitted Transfer"):**

> (a) any Transfer to an Affiliate of Tenant;

> (b) any Transfer to Coventry Capital Partners LP, its affiliates, related funds, or any entity managed or advised by Coventry Capital Partners LP or its affiliates, or to Marcus Ellison or his estate planning vehicles;

> (c) any grant of a Leasehold Mortgage, and any Transfer to or by a Leasehold Mortgagee or its designee, including any foreclosure, deed in lieu of foreclosure, assignment, or transfer in connection with the exercise of remedies;

> (d) any Transfer resulting from a merger, consolidation, or reorganization of Tenant, provided the surviving entity assumes this Lease;

> (e) any public offering, private placement, or transfer of direct or indirect equity interests in Tenant or any of its direct or indirect owners, including any transfer of limited partner interests, membership interests, or interests in a real estate investment trust, fund, or similar vehicle;

> (f) any Transfer to a Person that acquires all or substantially all of Tenant's assets or equity, provided such Person (i) has a tangible net worth of not less than the greater of (A) $75,000,000 and (B) the amount of Tenant's net worth at the time of the Transfer, and (ii) has, together with its affiliates, not less than ten (10) years' experience developing, owning, or operating mixed-use properties of comparable size in the Northeast;

> (g) any Transfer pursuant to a plan of reorganization, dissolution, or liquidation effected in compliance with Article 18; and

> (h) any Transfer to a governmental entity or authority.

**Section 18.4 Objective Qualification Standards.** For purposes of Section 17.8 and Section 18.3(f), a **"qualified transferee"** is a Person that (a) has a tangible net worth, determined in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, of not less than $75,000,000 (or, if the transferee is an institutional investor, managed funds or committed capital of not less than $250,000,000), (b) together with its affiliates has not less than ten (10) years' experience developing, owning, or operating mixed-use or multifamily properties of comparable size and quality, and (c) is not a Person with whom Landlord is prohibited from transacting business under applicable law.

**Section 18.5 Right of First Refusal.**

> (a) **Grant.** During the first twenty (20) years of the Term (that is, from the Lease Commencement Date through September 30, 2045), if Tenant proposes to Transfer this Lease to a Person that is not an Affiliate (and the proposed Transfer is not a Permitted Transfer), Landlord shall have a right of first refusal (the **"Right of First Refusal"**) to acquire the leasehold interest on the same terms and conditions as the proposed Transfer.

> (b) **Notice.** Tenant shall deliver to Landlord a written notice (an **"Assignment Notice"**) setting forth the identity of the proposed transferee, the material terms of the proposed Transfer (including price), and a copy of the proposed assignment agreement or letter of intent (redacted to remove confidential or competitively sensitive information).

> (c) **Exercise.** Landlord shall have sixty (60) days after receipt of the Assignment Notice to exercise the Right of First Refusal by written notice to Tenant. **If Landlord does not exercise within such period, or if Landlord exercises but fails to close within ninety (90) days thereafter (subject only to customary closing conditions), the Right of First Refusal shall lapse with respect to such proposed Transfer, and Tenant may proceed with the Transfer to the identified transferee on terms no more favorable to the transferee than those set forth in the Assignment Notice. If the Transfer does not close within one hundred eighty (180) days after the Assignment Notice, the Right of First Refusal shall be reinstated.**

> (d) **Exclusions.** **The Right of First Refusal shall not apply to, and shall be deemed waived with respect to, any Permitted Transfer, including without limitation any grant of a Leasehold Mortgage, any foreclosure, deed in lieu of foreclosure, or other exercise of remedies by a Leasehold Mortgagee, any assignment by a Leasehold Mortgagee or its designee, and any Transfer to an Affiliate.**

> (e) **No Restraint on Financing.** **Landlord acknowledges and agrees that the Right of First Refusal shall not apply to, delay, condition, or otherwise impair (i) the granting, recording, administration, enforcement, or foreclosure of any Leasehold Mortgage, (ii) any collateral assignment of leases and rents, (iii) any pledge of Tenant's direct or indirect ownership interests in favor of a Leasehold Mortgagee, or (iv) any Transfer effected in connection with any of the foregoing.** Any provision of this Lease or of any recorded instrument to the contrary shall not apply to the matters described in this Section 18.5(e), and Landlord shall be deemed to have waived the Right of First Refusal with respect to such matters.

**Section 18.6 Amendment of Recorded Right of First Refusal.** **The Parties acknowledge that the Declaration of Right of First Refusal dated September 8, 2019 and recorded at Volume 405, Page 55 of the Port Calloway Land Records (the "Recorded ROFR") does not, by its terms, contain any exception or carve-out for transfers resulting from foreclosure, deed in lieu of foreclosure, the exercise of remedies by a leasehold mortgagee, or assignments by a leasehold mortgagee or its designee following a foreclosure or acceptance of a deed in lieu. As a condition to the Lease Commencement Date, Landlord shall execute, acknowledge, and record an amendment to the Recorded ROFR (in form reasonably satisfactory to Tenant and each Leasehold Mortgagee) that (a) incorporates the exceptions set forth in Sections 18.3 and 18.5, (b) confirms that the Recorded ROFR applies only to a Transfer of this Lease and not to any Leasehold Mortgage, collateral assignment, or pledge, and (c) confirms that the Recorded ROFR will not be asserted against any Leasehold Mortgagee, any purchaser at foreclosure, any transferee under a deed in lieu of foreclosure, or any designee or affiliate of any of them. Landlord shall deliver such recorded amendment, together with evidence of recordation, on or before the Lease Commencement Date.**

**Section 18.7 Subletting.** Tenant may sublease or license space within the Project to residential, office, and retail tenants in the ordinary course of business without Landlord's consent. **A sublease of all or substantially all of the Premises to a single subtenant shall require Landlord's consent only if such sublease is for a term exceeding twenty-five (25) years, and in such case Landlord's consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed and Landlord may not exercise the Right of First Refusal in respect thereof. Landlord shall have no right to approve the identity, creditworthiness, or rent of any subtenant, or to review any sublease.**

**Section 18.8 No Release.** No Transfer shall release Tenant from its obligations under this Lease accruing prior to the Transfer, except that a Transfer of this Lease in compliance with this Article 18 shall release the transferor from obligations accruing after the date of the Transfer, provided the transferee assumes this Lease in writing.

**Section 18.9 Landlord's Transfer of Fee Interest.** Landlord may not transfer its fee interest in the Premises except subject to this Lease, and any transferee shall be deemed to have assumed Landlord's obligations under this Lease. Landlord shall deliver written notice to Tenant and each Leasehold Mortgagee within ten (10) Business Days after any transfer of its fee interest. **Landlord shall not be released from liability for obligations arising prior to the transfer.**

**Section 18.10 Right of First Opportunity to Purchase Fee.** **If at any time during the Term Landlord proposes to sell, convey, or otherwise dispose of its fee interest in the Premises to a Person other than a Governmental Authority, Tenant shall have a right of first opportunity to purchase the fee interest on the same terms as the proposed disposition, exercisable by written notice within thirty (30) days after receipt of Landlord's notice describing the proposed terms.** This Section 18.10 shall not apply to (a) any transfer to a Governmental Authority, (b) any transfer required by law, or (c) any encumbrance or mortgage.

# ARTICLE 19 — DEFAULT AND REMEDIES

**Section 19.1 Tenant Events of Default.** Each of the following is an **"Event of Default"** by Tenant:

> (a) **Monetary.** Failure by Tenant to pay any installment of Base Rent, Percentage Rent, or any other monetary obligation under this Lease when due, which failure continues for ten (10) Business Days after written notice from Landlord that such payment is past due;

> (b) **Non-Monetary.** Failure by Tenant to perform or observe any material non-monetary obligation under this Lease, which failure continues for thirty (30) days after written notice from Landlord specifying the failure in reasonable detail, or, if such failure cannot reasonably be cured within thirty (30) days, failure by Tenant to commence cure within such thirty (30) day period and thereafter diligently prosecute such cure to completion;

> (c) **Milestone.** Failure by Tenant to achieve Milestone 1 or Milestone 3, as extended, **subject to the Milestone Cure Period and the Mortgagee Cure Period and the provisions of Article 5, which shall govern exclusively with respect to such failure**;

> (d) **Insolvency.** The filing by Tenant of a voluntary petition in bankruptcy or seeking relief under any insolvency law, the entry of an order for relief against Tenant in an involuntary proceeding that is not dismissed within ninety (90) days, the making by Tenant of a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or the appointment of a receiver or trustee for Tenant or a substantial part of its assets that is not discharged within ninety (90) days; **provided that none of the foregoing shall constitute a basis for termination of this Lease unless and until the Leasehold Mortgagee has been afforded its rights under Sections 17.5, 17.6(f), and 17.9**;

> (e) **Abandonment.** Abandonment of the Premises by Tenant for a continuous period of one hundred eighty (180) days without payment of Rent and without the consent of Landlord, **other than during any period in which Tenant is prevented from operating by Casualty, Condemnation, Force Majeure, or a governmental order, or during construction**; and

> (f) **Misrepresentation.** Any material misrepresentation by Tenant in this Lease or in any certificate delivered under it, **provided that Landlord's sole remedy for a misrepresentation that is curable shall be specific performance and damages, and not termination**.

**Section 19.2 Landlord's Remedies.** Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an uncured Event of Default by Tenant, Landlord may exercise only the following remedies, which are **exclusive**:

> (a) terminate this Lease by written notice to Tenant and each Leasehold Mortgagee, subject to Article 5 (in the case of a Milestone failure) and Section 17.6 (in all cases);

> (b) recover from Tenant the amount of any Rent and other sums then due and unpaid, together with interest at the rate set forth in Section 6.8 and Landlord's reasonable costs of enforcement, including attorneys' fees;

> (c) draw upon the Security Deposit in accordance with Section 10.5;

> (d) seek specific performance of Tenant's obligations;

> (e) recover damages for the period prior to termination, **measured by the Rent and other sums due and unpaid and Landlord's documented out-of-pocket costs, and in no event including consequential, punitive, speculative, or indirect damages, or the loss of the value of the reversion**; and

> (f) exercise the Reverter Right in the case of a Milestone failure, strictly in accordance with Article 5.

**Landlord shall have no right (i) to accelerate Rent, (ii) to recover rent for any period after termination except as expressly permitted by applicable law and then only to the extent of Landlord's net loss after reasonable mitigation, (iii) to forfeit the Improvements, (iv) to levy against Tenant's personal property, or (v) to exercise any remedy not expressly set forth in this Section 19.2.**

**Section 19.3 Notice and Cure as Condition Precedent.** No Event of Default shall be deemed to exist, and Landlord shall have no right to exercise any remedy, unless Landlord has delivered the written notice required by Section 19.1 and the applicable cure period has expired without cure. **Delivery of a notice of default to Tenant without simultaneous delivery to each Leasehold Mortgagee shall be void.**

**Section 19.4 Landlord Events of Default.** Each of the following is an **"Event of Default"** by Landlord: (a) failure by Landlord to perform or observe any material obligation under this Lease, including any obligation under Article 3, Article 4, Article 5, Article 8, Article 9, or Article 17, which failure continues for thirty (30) days after written notice from Tenant specifying the failure, or, if such failure cannot reasonably be cured within thirty (30) days, failure by Landlord to commence cure within such period and thereafter diligently prosecute cure to completion; (b) any breach of Landlord's representations and warranties in Article 3 or Article 9; (c) any failure to pay an amount due to Tenant under this Lease within thirty (30) days after written demand; and (d) any transfer of the fee interest in violation of Section 3.9 or Section 18.9.

**Section 19.5 Tenant's Remedies.** Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an uncured Event of Default by Landlord, Tenant may exercise any or all of the following remedies, which are cumulative:

> (a) **Offset.** Offset against Base Rent, as an Express Offset, the amount of any damages, cost, or expense incurred by Tenant by reason of Landlord's default, including the cost of curing Landlord's default, together with interest at the rate set forth in Section 6.8;

> (b) **Self-Help.** Perform Landlord's obligation on Landlord's behalf, and charge the cost thereof to Landlord as an Express Offset, provided Tenant has given Landlord the notice and cure period required by Section 19.4 and Landlord has failed to perform;

> (c) **Specific Performance.** Seek specific performance of Landlord's obligations, and Landlord expressly agrees that its obligations under Article 3, Article 4, Article 5, Article 8, Article 9, Article 17, and Article 18 are specifically enforceable;

> (d) **Damages.** Recover damages, including consequential damages to the extent proximately caused by Landlord's default and reasonably foreseeable;

> (e) **Termination.** Terminate this Lease if Landlord's default is material and incapable of cure, or if Landlord fails to cure within ninety (90) days after notice, and in such event recover from Landlord the value of Tenant's leasehold estate, including the Appraised Value of the Improvements, as damages; and

> (f) **Suspension of Rent.** Suspend payment of Base Rent during the continuance of a Landlord default that renders the Premises untenantable or materially interferes with Tenant's construction or operation of the Project.

**Section 19.6 Landlord's Liability; No Limitation to Premises.** **Landlord's obligations under this Lease are full recourse obligations of Landlord, payable from all funds and assets available to Landlord, and are not limited to Landlord's interest in the Premises.** Landlord shall not assert, and hereby waives, any defense based on (a) the absence of an appropriation, (b) the lack of a budget line item, (c) governmental or sovereign immunity as to its contractual obligations, to the extent such immunity may be waived under applicable law, or (d) the public purpose of its functions. **Tenant's right of offset under Section 19.5(a) is expressly agreed by Landlord to be a permissible contractual remedy and shall not be subject to any statutory or municipal limitation on the attachment of public funds.**

**Section 19.7 Mitigation.** Both Parties shall use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate damages arising from the other's default. Landlord shall have no claim for damages in respect of any period during which Landlord has re-let or could reasonably have re-let the Premises, and any recovery by Landlord shall be reduced by the amount of rent Landlord receives or could reasonably have received.

**Section 19.8 Waiver; Notice of Default.** No waiver by either Party of any default shall be effective unless in writing and shall not be a waiver of any subsequent default. No delay or omission in exercising any right shall impair that right.

**Section 19.9 No Right of Re-Entry on Milestone Failure Without Article 5.** Nothing in this Article 19 shall be construed to permit Landlord to re-enter or take possession of the Premises, or to take title to the Improvements, on account of a Milestone failure except strictly in accordance with Article 5.

**Section 19.10 Force Majeure.** Neither Party shall be liable for any failure or delay in performance (other than the payment of money, except to the extent payment is excused by an Express Offset) caused by a Force Majeure Event (an **"Unavoidable Delay"**), provided the affected Party gives notice within a reasonable time and uses commercially reasonable efforts to resume performance. **Rent shall not abate by reason of a Force Majeure Event except as expressly provided in Article 15 and Article 16.**

# ARTICLE 20 — SURRENDER AND END OF TERM

**Section 20.1 Surrender at Expiration.** Upon the expiration of the Term on September 30, 2124, or upon any earlier termination of this Lease, Tenant shall surrender the Premises and the Improvements to Landlord in good condition and repair, reasonable wear and tear, Casualty, Condemnation, and Obsolescence excepted, free and clear of all liens and encumbrances created by Tenant (other than Permitted Exceptions and subleases permitted or approved under this Lease), and free of all occupants other than subtenants under subleases permitted under Article 18, which subleases shall be assigned to Landlord at Landlord's election without consideration.

**Section 24.3 Notices.** All notices, consents, demands, and other communications under this Lease shall be in writing and shall be deemed given (a) when delivered by hand, (b) one (1) Business Day after deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier, or (c) three (3) Business Days after deposit in the United States mail, certified or registered, return receipt requested, postage prepaid, addressed as follows (or to such other address as a Party designates by notice):

>
> **If to Tenant:** Meridian Gateway Holdings LLC, 400 Harborview Drive, Suite 1200, Port Calloway, CT 06801, Attention: Marcus Ellison, Managing Member, with a copy to Hargrove & Linden LLP, 1100 Constitution Avenue, Hartford, CT 06103, Attention: Rebecca Tsang, Esq.
>
> **If to a Leasehold Mortgagee:** at the address designated in accordance with Section 17.3.

**Section 24.5 Severability.** If any provision of this Lease is held invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect, and the invalid provision shall be reformed to the minimum extent necessary to make it enforceable while preserving the Parties' intent.

**Section 24.6 No Partnership.** Nothing in this Lease creates a partnership, joint venture, or principal-agent relationship between the Parties, and Landlord shall have no interest in the profits or losses of the Project except as expressly provided in Article 7.

**Section 24.7 Time of the Essence.** Time is of the essence with respect to each date and period set forth in this Lease, subject to Sections 4.3, 4.4, and 19.10.

**Section 24.8 Counterparts; Electronic Signatures.** This Lease may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one instrument. Electronic signatures shall be valid and binding.

# list styles font

"""Accept all tracked changes in a .docx by direct OOXML manipulation.

Usage: python accept_changes.py input.docx output.docx

Walks word/document.xml: unwraps <w:ins> elements (keeps their content) and
removes <w:del> elements (drops their content). No LibreOffice needed.
"""
import sys
import tempfile
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

from lxml import etree


W_NS = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main"
NSMAP = {"w": W_NS}


def accept(input_path: Path, output_path: Path):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as workdir:
        wd = Path(workdir)
        with zipfile.ZipFile(input_path) as z:
            z.extractall(wd)

        for doc_xml in wd.rglob("document*.xml"):
            if "/word/" not in doc_xml.as_posix():
                continue
            tree = etree.parse(str(doc_xml))

            # Accept insertions: unwrap <w:ins> (move children up)
            for ins in tree.findall(".//w:ins", NSMAP):
                parent = ins.getparent()
                if parent is None:
                    continue
                idx = list(parent).index(ins)
                for child in list(ins):
                    parent.insert(idx, child)
                    idx += 1
                parent.remove(ins)

            # Reject deletions: drop entire <w:del> elements
            for d in tree.findall(".//w:del", NSMAP):
                parent = d.getparent()
                if parent is not None:
                    parent.remove(d)

            tree.write(
                str(doc_xml),
                xml_declaration=True, encoding="UTF-8", standalone=True,
            )

        output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with zipfile.ZipFile(output_path, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zout:
            for p in sorted(wd.rglob("*")):
                if p.is_file():
                    zout.write(p, p.relative_to(wd).as_posix())

    print(f"OK: wrote {output_path}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
        print("Usage: accept_changes.py <input.docx> <output.docx>", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(2)
    accept(Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2]))

{"command": "cd /workspace/work && cat > memo.md << 'XEOF'
---
title: "MEMORANDUM"
subtitle: "Privileged and Confidential — Attorney Work Product — Attorney-Client Communication"
---

| | |
|:--|:--|
| **TO:** | Marcus Ellison, Managing Member, Meridian Gateway Holdings LLC |
| **CC:** | Ansel Coventry III, Managing Partner, Coventry Capital Partners LP |
| **FROM:** | Rebecca Tsang, Partner; Jordan Abernathy, Associate — Hargrove & Linden LLP |
| **DATE:** | June 27, 2025 |
| **RE:** | First Draft Ground Lease — Drafting Issues, Document Conflicts, and Gap Analysis (10-30 Pier Street, Port Calloway, CT; APN 127-003-0045) |

# I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

**1. Purpose and deliverable.** This memorandum accompanies the first draft of the Ground Lease Agreement (the **"Draft Lease"**) for the Authority-owned waterfront parcel at 10-30 Pier Street. You asked us to (a) prepare a first draft keyed to your four stated priorities, and (b) identify every issue, conflict, and gap across the executed Term Sheet, the Ridgepoint Title Commitment No. TC-2025-07821, the Halcyon Phase II Environmental Site Assessment, the Bayside Federal construction loan term sheet, and the Authority's Resolution No. 2025-047 — "not just the ones I've flagged." We have done both. The Draft Lease is 78 pages and contains 24 Articles and 12 Exhibits. This memorandum is the issue log and should be read alongside it.

**2. Headline.** The transaction is draftable and the Draft Lease is financeable in form. But **three defects in the record as it stands are capable of stopping the deal on their own**, independent of the reverter: the Title Commitment's legal description does not describe the parcel the survey describes (it describes roughly twice as much land); the recorded 2019 Right of First Refusal contains no exception for mortgagee transfers and will therefore fail Bayside's checklist as written; and the Bayside term sheet is an expressly non-binding document that expired on June 27, 2025. Each is fixable, but each requires action by the Authority or a third party, not by us.

**3. Top risk register.** Ranked by the probability that the item alone prevents the October 1, 2025 Lease Commencement Date.

| # | Issue | Why it can stop the deal | Owner |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **1** | **Title Commitment Exhibit A describes a different (and twice as large) parcel.** Its metes and bounds compute to 279,535 SF (6.417 acres) against the stated 139,392 SF (3.2 acres), and close at 1:1,927 rather than the 1:15,000 the surveyor certified. | The ALTA leasehold policies and the Leasehold Mortgage cannot be issued against a description that does not match the insured land, and Tenant may be leasing the wrong legal parcel. | Ridgepoint / Authority |
| **2** | **Recorded Right of First Refusal (Vol. 405, Pg. 55) has no foreclosure carve-out.** The title company says so expressly (Exception No. 4). | Bayside requires an unconditional right to foreclose and assign without Landlord consent (§5.6). A recorded ROFR that arguably captures a foreclosure transfer defeats that right, and no construction lender will close against it. | Authority (record an amendment) |
| **3** | **No binding financing commitment exists.** The Bayside term sheet is non-binding except §§11–12 and expired by its terms on June 27, 2025. | Every deliverable in the Lease assumes a $285M loan that has not been committed. The Lease should not be executed before the loan is committed, and the schedule is built on an assumption we cannot verify. | Client / Bayside |
| **4** | **Reverter forfeiture.** The Term Sheet extinguishes $200–300M of Improvements with no compensation and also forfeits the $5.7M LOC. | It is the issue you identified, and it is also Bayside's stated deal-breaker. We have drafted a compliant alternative (Article 5). The Authority's Resolution §2(a) requires a reverter, so this will need Board approval of the final form. | Joint |
| **5** | **Tax abatement has no instrument and no authority identified.** The abatement must be implemented by the *City*, which is not a party to the Lease, and no draft agreement, Board of Finance authorization, or statutory basis appears in the record. | §4.2 of the project economics (§1.55M–$4.6M per year) rests on an incentive that is not yet legally committed. | City / Authority |
| **6** | **Tax abatement clock starts at the wrong time.** As written in the Term Sheet it burns three construction years of the 15-year benefit and overstates Tenant's taxes by roughly $1.40M per year *on a vacant lot*. | Quantified at **$4,201,275** of lost benefit; Coventry's model assumes the full 15 years during the income-producing period. | Joint |
| **7** | **ELUR ground-floor prohibition vs. the Project's lobby, amenity, leasing and fitness program.** Halcyon flags the ambiguity and recommends a DEEP interpretation; the Term Sheet permits the very uses in question. | A DEEP enforcement action against a 28-story residential tower is an existential operating risk, and Bayside's condition (e) requires Lender's consultant to confirm consistency. | Authority / DEEP |
| **8** | **The Bulkhead.** Fair-to-poor condition, ~480 LF, no cost estimate in the record, excluded from the $2.4M remediation estimate, not allocated by the Term Sheet, and described inconsistently in three documents. | A waterfront tower cannot obtain a certificate of occupancy behind a failing bulkhead. Unallocated, this is a $5M–$15M hole in the budget. | Joint |
| **9** | **"Lease Year" is never defined, and three competing clocks run off different events.** | Base rent escalation, the tax abatement, and percentage rent all key off "Year," which the Term Sheet measures from Lease Commencement in §10 and from Rent Commencement in §§5–6. The difference is worth roughly two years of escalation. | Drafting (resolved in Draft Lease) |
| **10** | **Percentage rent breakpoint is fixed at $28.5M for 99 years** with none of the indexation that every other rent component has. | Your concern is correct and quantifiable; by Year 96 the breakpoint retains roughly 4% of its 2025 purchasing power. We have indexed it (Article 7). | Joint |

**4. What is *not* broken.** We recomputed every figure, date, and cross-reference in the record. Base rent, the escalation steps, the remediation credit arithmetic, the LOC amounts, the sources-and-uses, the assessed-value tax calculations, and all four milestone dates reconcile (see Part III). The parties, entity identifiers, addresses, and counsel are consistent throughout. The problems in this file are not arithmetic errors; they are *definitional gaps, unallocated risks, and third-party consents*.

**5. Recommendation.** Transmit the Draft Lease to Howard Koss on Monday, and in the same transmittal letter (a) request the 2012 Final Judgment of Condemnation and the recorded subdivision or lot-line instrument establishing the APN 127-003-0045 / 127-003-0044 boundary, (b) request that Ridgepoint conform Exhibit A to its commitment, (c) request that the Authority agree to record amendments to the 2019 ROFR and the 2019 affordable housing declaration, and (d) confirm the status of the Bayside commitment. We should not let the two-week drafting deadline drive us into a transmittal that does not put those four items on the table in writing.

# II. SCOPE, SOURCES, AND WHAT THE RECORD DOES NOT CONTAIN

**1. Sources reviewed in full.**

| Document | Date | Status / weight |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Ground Lease Term Sheet | June 10, 2025 | Executed; binding only as to exclusivity and good-faith negotiation (Term Sheet §19) |
| Bayside Federal Construction Loan Term Sheet | May 28, 2025 | **Non-binding** except §§11–12; expired June 27, 2025; acceptance block undated in our copy |
| Ridgepoint Title Commitment TC-2025-07821 | Effective June 1, 2025 | Binding offer to insure, subject to Requirements and Exceptions; **expires December 1, 2025** |
| Halcyon Phase II ESA — Executive Summary | May 2, 2025 | Executive summary only; appendices under separate cover |
| Calloway Land Surveyors — ALTA/NSPS Survey narrative | Plat April 28, 2025 | Narrative and legal description only; plat sheets not in the file |
| Authority Resolution No. 2025-047 | Adopted June 5, 2025 | Certification block blank; vote count not filled in |
| Client instructions (e-mail) | June 15, 2025 | Statement of client objectives; not a source of deal terms |

**2. Documents that are referenced but not in the file.** Each is a condition to something in the Draft Lease. The bracketed item is who we believe holds it.

> (a) 2012 Final Judgment of Condemnation — cited in the Title Commitment as **Volume 367, Page 44** but in the Survey as **Volume 375, Page 44** ("Final Order of Condemnation"); the discrepancy must be resolved. [Ridgepoint / Authority]
>
> (b) Any recorded subdivision map, lot-line revision, or deed establishing the boundary between APN 127-003-0045 and APN 127-003-0044. None is referenced anywhere in the record. [Authority / Assessor]
>

# IV. DETAILED ISSUE ANALYSIS

## A. The Premises: The Title Commitment Describes a Different Parcel

**The issue.** Exhibit A to Title Commitment TC-2025-07821 contains a five-course metes and bounds description that does not describe the 3.2-acre parcel it says it describes.

**The record.** The commitment's Exhibit A runs: (1) N 72°15'30" E, 580.00'; (2) S 18°22'45" E, 240.40'; (3) S 17°48'10" E, 239.60'; (4) S 72°08'15" W, 582.50'; (5) N 17°44'30" W, 480.20'. The Survey's description runs: S 78°15'30" E, 435.22'; S 11°44'30" W, 320.47'; N 78°15'30" W, 435.22'; N 11°44'30" E, 320.47'. Every element differs: the bearings (72° vs. 78°; 17° vs. 11°), both dimensions (580' vs. 435.22'; 480.20' vs. 320.47'), and the resulting area.

**Why it matters.** We closed both descriptions. The Survey description is a true rectangle that closes exactly and computes to 139,475 SF (3.202 ac) — consistent with the stated 139,392 SF within rounding. The Commitment description computes to **279,535 SF (6.417 acres)** — almost exactly double — and closes at a precision of **1:1,927**, which fails the 1:15,000 standard the surveyor certified and which no title company would accept as an insurable description of a metes-and-bounds parcel. Three consequences follow:

> (1) **The commitment may be insuring the wrong land.** If the policy describes the 6.417-acre figure, it insures land the Authority does not intend to lease, or the Authority does not own free of the park parcel.
>
> (2) **The APN boundary may have no record basis.** The most likely explanation is that the commitment's description is the description of the *parent tract* the Authority took by condemnation in 2012, from which APN 127-003-0044 was later carved out on the tax maps. But an assessor's parcel number is a taxing designation, not a legal lot. **No subdivision map, lot-line revision, or deed dividing 127-003-0045 from 127-003-0044 appears anywhere in the record.** If no such instrument exists, then the southern boundary of the Premises — which runs 435.22 feet and abuts the Authority's own retained park parcel — is a tax-map line with no record support, and the Authority may be purporting to lease a parcel it has not legally created.
>
> (3) **The surveyor attribution is also inconsistent.** The commitment attributes its description to a survey by "Calloway Land Surveyors LLC, J. Michael Ferreira, P.L.S., Connecticut License No. 12847 … dated April 20, 2025, and last revised May 15, 2025, Drawing No. CLS-2025-0321." The Survey in our file is by **Thomas R. Pellegrino, PLS, License No. PLS-008741, Job No. CLS-2025-0417**, field survey April 20, 2025, plat April 28, 2025. Different surveyor, different license number, different job number, different final date. Either a second survey exists that we have never seen, or the commitment contains a transcription error in both the narrative and the attribution.

**Recommendation.** (a) Send a title objection under Section 3.4 of the Draft Lease requiring the Issuing Title Company to conform its commitment and both policies to Exhibit A to the Lease, and to identify by volume and page the record instrument that creates the southern boundary. (b) Request the 2012 Final Judgment of Condemnation — noting that the Commitment cites **Vol. 367, Pg. 44** while the Survey cites **Vol. 375, Pg. 44** for what appears to be the same 2012 judgment. (c) Ask the Authority to confirm whether the 2012 taking included both parcels, and, if so, that a subdivision or lot-line revision was recorded. (d) Do not accept a "same as survey" endorsement as a substitute; the description itself must be corrected.

**Draft treatment.** Sections 2.2(b) and (c), 3.4 and Exhibit A (with the drafting note retained for negotiation), and conditions precedent §2.5(b) and (c).

## B. The Reverter and Forfeiture — The Hill

### 1. What the Term Sheet actually says

Section 9 of the Term Sheet provides that if Tenant misses Milestone 1 or Milestone 3, Landlord "may exercise a reverter right by delivering written notice"; Tenant then has 180 days to cure; and if it fails, "**the Lease shall automatically terminate**," whereupon (a) Tenant forfeits the entire $5,700,000 LOC, which Landlord "shall be entitled to draw in full," and (b) all Improvements "shall immediately revert to and become the sole property of the Landlord, free and clear of any claims by Tenant, **without any payment, compensation, or reimbursement to Tenant**."

**Three internal defects, independent of the policy question:**

> (i) **"May exercise" vs. "shall automatically terminate."** The mechanism is both elective and automatic. Landlord's counsel will read the automatic language to mean no notice is required; our reading is that the elective language controls. This ambiguity alone will produce litigation at the worst possible moment. The Draft Lease (§5.1) resolves it by making every step conditional and requiring an express payment as a condition to effectiveness.
